This being established, I say first that the Egyptians were the first of all mortals to divide the sky into 48 images, according to the testimony of Hyginus <note>Gaius Julius Hyginus, a Roman mythographer and astronomer</note>. He says, *"The signs and images by which the stars and planets are marked by astronomers are Chaldean and Egyptian."* This division was appropriately made so that 24 images were placed under the South and just as many under the North; all of these they called the "stations of the Gods" or "dwellings of the Gods," as we have said. For they placed a certain *choragus* <note>A leader or conductor of a group</note> over each individual image, to whom the remaining stars of one and the same constellation were joined like attendants. To each one they assigned a certain protection over things contained in the lower world, and they declared that man blessed who could understand the "chains" of these constellations, by which the corresponding and matching Classes in the lower world were connected. For once these were known, they thought it would not be difficult to attract good Spirits <note>original: "Genios"</note> appropriate to each matter into one's own affairs—whether through sacrifices or various compositions taken from the aforementioned classes of natural things—and to drive away the malignant ones through the customary rites. For as Ptolemy rightly says: *"The faces of this lower world are subject to the celestial faces."* In the midst of these Divinities they placed Mithras, whom they also called the <term>Mesites</term> <note>original: "Μεσιτην", meaning "The Mediator"</note>, that is, the Sun. He acts like a Leader and supreme Monarch of the celestial world with the rest of the company of planets, returning now to the South, now to the North, visiting the subsidiary forces of the said Divinities every year, and by his power inciting each one to strengthen the preservation of the world's economy. Since all these matters have been established with their own authorities in the *Pamphilian Obelisk* on page 157, we refer the curious reader there. The Greeks followed them later, and because they did not understand the hieroglyphic images of the Egyptians, they converted them into the portraits of Gods of their own invention, which posterity has used even to this day. However, so that you may more clearly compare the original face of the sky as described hieroglyphically by the Egyptians with the portraits of the Greeks, we shall first place here both Hemispheres marked with the constellations of the Greeks, and then we shall place the portraits of the Egyptians.

->The Northern Portraits of the Greeks. 21 Northern Signs.<-

I. **The Lesser Bear**, *Helice* or *Cynosura*; Arabic: *Alracaba* <note>original: "الركبه"</note>; Greek: *Plastrum* <note>original: "ἅμαξα", meaning "The Wagon"</note>; Hebrew: *The Hen with her children* <note>original: "עיש ובניו", Gnasch</note>. It contains 21 stars and occupies Gemini, Cancer, and Leo; it is of the nature of Mars and Venus.

II. **The Greater Bear**, Greek: *The Greater Chariot* <note>original: "ἅμαξα μεγάλη"</note>; Arabic: *The Great Bear* <note>original: "الدبه الاكبر", Dubbe ellekbar</note>; Hebrew: *The Great Bear* <note>original: "דוב גדול"</note>; to the Indians, *The Golden Sea*. It contains 57 stars and occupies Leo, Virgo, and Libra; it is of a Martial nature.

III. **The Dragon**, Greek: *The Serpent* <note>original: "δράκων"</note>, *Python*; Arabic: *Tarban* <note>original: "ثعبان"</note>; Hebrew: *The Snake* <note>original: "תנין", Tanin</note>. It contains 32 stars and occupies Sagittarius, Capricorn, Aquarius, Pisces, Aries, Taurus, Gemini, Cancer, Leo, and Virgo; it is of the nature of Jupiter and Saturn.

IV. **Cepheus**, to the Greeks: *Kepheus* <note>original: "Κηφεύς"</note>; to the Arabs: *Keiphus* <note>original: "قيفوس"</note>; to the Hebrews: *The Lady of Flame* or *The Inflamed One* <note>original: "בעלת להב"</note>. It contains 13 stars and occupies Aries, Taurus, and Gemini; it is of the nature of Jupiter and Saturn.

XIII. **Ophiuchus**, or the Serpent-Bearer; Arabic: *Elhaui*, corrupted to *elangui*; Hebrew: *holding the living creatures* <note>original: עוצרת חיות</note>. It contains 24 stars and occupies the signs of Scorpio ♏ and Sagittarius ♐; it is of a Saturnine-Venusian nature.

XIV. **The Serpent of Ophiuchus**, in Greek: *Ophis*; Hebrew: *Hachaia*, *the serpent*; the same in Arabic: *Elhiuan*. It contains 13 stars and occupies the signs of Scorpio ♏, Sagittarius ♐, and Capricorn ♑; it is of a Martial-Saturnine nature.

XV. **The Arrow**, or the dart; in Greek: *Oistos*; Arabic: *Schaham*; Hebrew: *Satan, the Demon* <note>original: שטן</note>. It contains 8 stars and occupies Capricorn ♑; it is of a Martial-Venusian nature.

XVI. **The Eagle** or the Flying Vulture; in Greek: *Aetos*, or *the bird of Jove*; Arabic: *Altair*; Hebrew: *Nescher*. It contains 19 stars including Antinous <note>Antinous was a sub-constellation formerly associated with Aquila</note> and occupies the sign of Capricorn ♑; it is of a Jovial-Martial nature.

XVII. **The Dolphin**, the carrier of Arion; in Greek: *Delphis*; Arabic: *Delphin*; Hebrew: *fish of the sea* <note>original: דג הים</note>. It contains 10 stars and occupies the sign of Aquarius ♒; it is of a Saturnine-Martial nature.

XVIII. **The Little Horse**, in Greek: *the section of the smaller horse*; Arabic: *Alshares elmek*; Hebrew: *head of the horse* <note>original: ראש חסוס</note>. It contains 4 stars and occupies the sign of Aquarius ♒; it is of a Martial-Jovial nature.

<margin>CHAPTER VII.</margin>

XLVI. The Censer <note>original: "Thuribulum"</note>, in Greek *thymiaterion*, the Altar; in Hebrew *machtat*, that is, *The Censer*. It contains 7 stars and occupies Scorpio; it is of the nature of Venus and Mercury.

XLVIII. The Southern Fish, or *Notius*; in Greek *ichthys megas*, *monazon*, *notios* <note>meaning the great, solitary, southern fish</note>. In Hebrew *dag dromi*, *The Southern Fish*. It contains 17 stars and occupies Aquarius and Pisces.

And these are the 48 Images with which the Greeks, led by mystical reasons, marked the entire sky; which indeed, as will be seen later, they borrowed from the Egyptians and, having adorned them with various fables, made their own. Let us now reveal what those primeval images were with which the Egyptians honored the heavens.

# CHAPTER VII.

->*How and why the Egyptians divided the Heaven into 48 Asterisms.*<-

<margin>The Egyptians believed that Gods or Spirits inhabited the stars.</margin>

It is a dogma of the Egyptians that celestial Gods or Spirits <note>original: "Genios"</note> inhabit the stars; for they thought the lower world subsisted by their power and efficacy—not by some inherent force of the stars' influence, but by the governing power of the Divinities <note>original: "Numinum"</note>. These, sitting in the stars as if upon a royal throne, would use the natural power of the stars as a kind of instrument for the arrangement of lower things. They taught that in each individual constellation <term>asterism|a group of stars forming a recognized pattern</term> a certain primary Divinity resided, while in the remaining stars belonging to the same constellation, Spirits resided as followers and ministers of the principal Divinity. They believed their power flowed down in a pyramidal influence, the base of which was defined by the size of the constellation itself, and the peak at the center of the earth. They called these the *archas* or "strongholds" of the Gods: for they judged that everything contained within such pyramids was subject to their power and arrangement. We have already discussed the twelve Divinities of the Zodiac at length in Chapter Five; it remains for us to discuss the rest of the constellations, both northern and southern, with equal pace. So that this may be done with greater method, it seemed best in the first place to show the arrangement of the <term>Iconisms|symbolic or pictorial representations</term> according to the three "faces" of each sign, following the mind of Avenar <note>Abraham ibn Ezra, a famous medieval Jewish scholar and astrologer</note> the Hebrew Astrologer, and the Indians.

->*The arrangement of the Iconisms, by which the Egyptians (according to the mind of Avenar) subdivided the twelve parts of the individual signs into three faces, and assigned appropriate Images to each face.*<-

The ancient Astrologers, as was said in the preceding pages, divided the Zodiac into 12 signs, which they called the strongholds of the Gods, and each one...

# CLASS VII. HIEROGLYPHIC MATHEMATICS. CHAPTER VII.

They distributed the twelve signs again into three parts, which they called "faces" or "countenances," but which the Moderns have named <term>Decans</term> <note>From the Greek 'deka' (ten), referring to the ten-degree subdivisions of a thirty-degree zodiacal sign</note>; they did this so that they attributed ten degrees to each individual face. To these faces or countenances they attached certain "Iconisms" or images, through which the nature of the influence active in such-and-such a face would be expressed by a certain symbolic sketch. For they predicted that from such-and-such a rising face, the future condition of a person's birth would be exactly as the symbolic constitution of the image had expressed. These images are to be conceived not only according to the length of the Zodiac, but also according to its width, so that, for example, all those images found within a rhombus formed by two lines marking the boundaries of a face and meeting at each pole are considered to belong to that face which the said two lines enclose. 

It should also be noted that there is a significant difference between these "iconisms" and the "asterisms" <note>constellations</note>, of which the Ancients established 48 in the heavens. For the iconisms of the faces were considered according to the width of the Zodiac, while the asterisms were considered according to the width of the equator. Since authors everywhere confuse the former with the latter, they have given occasion for the greatest perplexity. I believe this confusion arose because later Egyptians, introducing various new schemes into the heavens and repeatedly adding new ones to the original iconisms, gradually filled the entire sky with innumerable characterizations of monsters, just as they filled the minds of later astrologers with utter confusion. Therefore, so that we might avoid these sorts of quicksands, we shall first and separately exhibit the images of the faces just as <margin>Rabbi Aben Ezra, Beneka the Indian, Abenragel.</margin> Rabbi Aben Ezra <note>original: "R. Auenar"</note>, Beneka the Indian, and Abenragel the Arab described them, following the Egyptian tradition; then we shall also exhibit, side by side, the 48 star-bearing iconisms which the ancient authority of the Sages consecrated for posterity as specimens of primordial wisdom. Thus, Aben Ezra says:

->And in Aries, there rises in its first face the form of a woman who is<-
->as if in a flame, and a fish of the sea in the likeness of a serpent, and a triangular head.<-
<note>original Hebrew: "ובטלה עלה בפנים הראשונים ממנו צורת אשה היא במאירה ודג מים כדמות צפעה וראש משולש"</note>

<margin>The first face of the signs (Decans).</margin> And in the first face of Aries there rises the figure of a woman as if shimmering with fire, and a fish from the sea in the likeness of a serpent, and the head of a triangle or <term>Delta</term> <note>The Greek letter Δ, often associated with the Nile Delta or geometric divinity</note> are placed in the second face of <term>Ammon</term> <note>The ram-headed Egyptian deity Jupiter-Ammon, associated here with Aries</note>. These agree with the words of Beneka the Indian Gymnosophist <note>A "naked philosopher" or ascetic of ancient India</note>, whose words the cited Hebrew astrologer Aben Ezra recites. He describes the second face thus:

->And there rises in the second face a woman with a comb on her head and a scepter<-
->of copper, and the head of the Devil; and the people of India say that there rises there the form of<-
->a woman wrapped in clothes, who has one foot in the shape of<-
->an eagle.<-
<note>original Hebrew: "ויעלה בפנים השנים אשה יש מסרק בראשה ושרביט נחושת וראש השטן ויאמרו אנשי הודו כי יעלה שם צורת אשה מתעטפת בבגדים ויש לה רגל אחת וצורתה צורת הנשר"</note>

<margin>The second face.</margin> And there ascends in the second face the figure of a woman, on whose head is a comb, and a copper rod in her hand, and the head of the Devil; and the Indians think that a woman wrapped in garments ascends there, whose foot is of an Aquiline <note>eagle-like</note> shape. And in this manner they represented that deity <term>Nephten</term> <note>Nephthys, the Egyptian goddess</note> as an attendant, as will be shown in its proper place from the <term>Bembine Tablet</term> <note>An elaborate bronze tablet of Egyptian style, famous in the Renaissance as a key to hieroglyphs</note>.

# CHAPTER VI. 202 EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

->And in the third face there rises a youth sitting upon a throne, covered by a veil, and in his hand are Teraphim.<-

<margin>The third face.</margin>
And in the third face <note>original: "facie," referring to a decan or 10-degree division of a zodiac sign</note> there rises a youth sitting upon a draped seat, and in his hand are Teraphim. What is understood by "Teraphim" was declared at length in the first volume, Synthesis 3, in the chapter on the Baalim; for it was an averting idol <note>a protective talisman used to ward off evil</note> which the Egyptians used to carry with them. But see the cited location regarding these matters. This is followed by another kneeling image, which Ibn Ezra <note>original: "Auenar," referring to the Jewish scholar Abraham ibn Ezra</note> describes from the Astrology of the Egyptians in these words:

->And a man lowered his head downward and he cries out to the Name [God].<-

There also rises a man, bowing his head toward the lower parts, and suppliantly invoking God. This image is indeed nothing other than the image of a Tutelary Genius <note>a guardian spirit</note>, supplicating a superior power; it is found everywhere among the hieroglyphics and is often confused with the "Kneeler" <note>original: "Engoniasi," the constellation Hercules</note> among the Greek star-groups.

<margin>Attendants of Apis, or the Bull. 2</margin>
Within the kingdom of Apis <note>the Bull/Taurus</note> there first ascend, according to Egyptian Astrology, the image of a man holding a sword in his left hand and a staff in his right; then truly a great Ship, upon which is a Lion. But let us hear the words of Ibn Ezra:

->And there rises in the first face of the Bull a hero who has a sword in his left hand, and there also rises a great ship in which there is a lion.<-

In this place, Ibn Ezra confuses the figures of the faces with the constellations themselves. What is indicated by the Giant, if not Orion? What by the Ship, if not that most celebrated *Baris* <note>an Egyptian sacred boat</note>, marked with a leonine figure, which we call *Mophta*, and which is wrongly confused in this place with the Ship of the Argonauts? The Indians, in place of the Lion positioned in the Ship, place a Ram; which beautifully fits the figure of the Ram placed in the Ship on the Bembine Tablet <note>a famous bronze tablet of Isiac mysteries</note>. Furthermore, the Astrologers of the Indians say that beneath the Ship is the half of a dead woman. This is an error; for the Egyptians placed Horus in this spot, drowned in the Nile by Typhon, in whose place the Greeks substituted Icarus drowned in the Eridanus. Again, in the Northern face they say a man rises in Goat-like dress; by which nothing else is indicated but Erichthonius, weighed down by the weight of a kid. In the third face of Apis, there first rises Anubis, distinguished by his canine face, according to the testimony of Ibn Ezra, in whose hand is a serpent.

<margin>Attendants of the Twins. 3</margin>
In the first face of the Twins <note>Gemini</note> there likewise rises a figure transformed with a canine head, and it corresponds to the Little Dog or the Sirius of the Greeks, which the Egyptians call sometimes <term>aselgeon</term> <note>original: "ἀσέלγεον," likely a corruption of a term for "lustful" or "bright"</note>, and sometimes <term>seirion</term> <note>original: "σείריון," the Greek name for the Dog Star</note>. Again, within this space there also rises an erect serpent, and a wolf having a mark in its hand:

->And there rises there a beast standing upon a tree, and a wolf that has a sign in its hand, and a man who has a musical instrument of gold and he plays music upon it.<-

There rises there a Serpent dwelling in a tree, and a Wolf in whose hand is a sign, and a man in whose hand is a musical instrument with which he sings psalms. In place of the Wolf, the Greeks here place the beast of the Centaur; in place of the Musician, they place the Lyre.

<margin>Attendants of the Cancer and the Lion. 4</margin>
In the house of Cancer and the Lion there rise the Great and Little Bears, the true insignia of the Typhonian Kingdom, of which Hermes himself makes mention in the *Pymander* <note>a foundational text of Hermeticism</note>.

# CLASS VII. HIEROGLYPHIC MATHEMATICS 203 CHAPTER VI.

...he describes in these words: For the Bears, that is, the Great and Little Bears themselves which you know, never rise nor set, but perpetually recur around the same point. Although others place an iron pig with a copper head in the location of the Great Bear; the Egyptians more correctly place a greater and lesser chariot, as was said above; others place a serpent-footed man entwined with snakes, the kind of Typhon <note>A monstrous giant in Greek mythology associated with chaos and storms</note> we displayed in Volume One, Treatise 3, in the Chapter on Typhon. Whatever the case may be, all these symbols indicate something of a Typhonic nature.

<margin>Associated with Virgo and Libra.</margin>
5 Within the mansions of Virgo and Libra, a great Asp rises, which is also called the Ophionian Agathodæmon <note>Literally "Good Spirit of the Serpent"; a protective deity in Hellenistic and Egyptian religion</note>, together with a wine bowl, according to the testimony of Avenar <note>Abraham ibn Ezra, a famous 12th-century Jewish scholar and astrologer</note>. However, the Indian astrologers place a large tree in this location, in whose branches a Dog and an Ibis exist. But let us hear the words of the Author:

->And there ascends there a great tree, upon its branches a dog and a bird called the Rachamah.<-

> *There ascends there a great tree, in whose branches are a Dog and a Stork, which is also called an Ibis, and is named "Rachama" by the Hebrews out of "Philostorgia" <note>Greek for "parental love," referring to the stork's reputation for devotion to its young</note>.*

And this indicates nothing other than the station of the Mercurial Divinities. Furthermore, the Egyptians say (according to Avenar) that a beautiful virgin is placed in this location, remarkable for the length of her hair, holding two ears of grain in her hand; she sits upon a throne and suckles a tiny boy, nourishing him with the greatest care. Truly, since the words of Avenar are most worthy of consideration, I cite them here:

<margin>The Virgin suckling a boy in the Zodiac according to the opinion of the Egyptians and Hebrews.</margin>
->And there shall ascend in the first face a beautiful virgin with long hair, and in her hand two ears of grain; and she sits upon a throne and shall raise a small child, and suckle him and feed him.<-

> *In the first face <note>A "face" or "decan" is a 10-degree subdivision of a zodiac sign</note> of Virgo, he says, there ascends a beautiful Virgin with long hair; she holds two ears of grain in her hand, sits upon a seat, and nourishes a boy who is still tiny, and suckles him, and feeds him.*

Albumazar <note>A famous 9th-century Persian astrologer</note> describes these things much more expressly in his *Introduction to Astrology*, which words Stofflerus quotes in his *Sphere of Proclus*; he discusses it thus: There rises in the first decan of Virgo a girl, called in Arabic <margin>* corrupted</margin> *Aderenosa*, that is, a Pure Virgin, an Immaculate Virgin, beautiful in body, lovely in countenance, modest in habit, with long hair, holding two ears of grain in her two hands, residing upon a canopied floor, nourishing and rightly feeding a boy, whose name is Hebrew—I say a boy named by certain nations **Jesus**, signifying *Issa*, whom the Greeks also call **Christ**. Thus says Albumazar. From these things it is clearly evident that our Savior, born of the unstained Virgin, is indicated. Therefore, this Virgin rises feeding **JESUS**. Let the stubborn Hebrews be ashamed here, while they reject the Virgin Mother, when the Gentiles foresaw these things for so many ages, so many centuries before them. But if a "Circumcised One" <note>original: "Verpus," a derogatory term for a circumcised man, here used for a Jewish skeptic</note> should say: *They do not say this Virgin is the mother of that boy, but only that she is rightly feeding him*; let the unhappy man blush, because she who rightly feeds him is none other than the mother. Something similar is read in the European Sibyl: *He shall come leaping over mountains and hills, and reigning in poverty with the silence of ruling, he shall spring forth from the vessel of the Virgin.* There is also placed in this same location by the Egyptians the figure of a man <term>Tauromorphos</term> <note>original: Ταυρομόρφος</note>, that is, of a Bull-like form. So says Avenar:

<margin>Attendants of Sagittarius and Capricorn.</margin>
7 Within the latitude of Sagittarius and Capricorn, between the South and North, the Egyptians place the figure of a young goat holding horns; and this is the same figure which we explained above in the sign of Capricorn. Next is the figure of a flying Hawk; and in the place of the Hawk, the Greeks later substituted a flying Eagle. Furthermore, in this space the Egyptians place a <term>Cynocephalus</term> <note>original Greek: Κυνοκέφαλον</note>, that is, the body of an Ape with a dog's head. Thus <term>Auenar</term> <note>Abraham ibn Ezra, a 12th-century scholar</note> teaches from the Astrology of the Egyptians:

->And there shall rise there the body of an ape and its head is like the head of a dog.<-

*And there rises in that same place the body of an Ape, and its head is like the head of a Dog.* Concerning this Dog-headed figure and its significance, see the *Pamphilian Obelisk*, Book 3, under the Hieroglyphic Symbolism of the Ape.

<margin>Attendants of Aquarius and Pisces.</margin>
8 Within the station of Aquarius and Pisces they place a Hen with chicks. The <term>Oxyrhynchus</term> fish <note>A sacred Nile fish</note> and the figure of the Nile.

And these are the images which Auenar reports were inserted into the heavens according to the mind of the Egyptians—symbols of hidden actions, which the Greeks then polished and adorned with their own fables and handed down to posterity; I have thought it right to set them down here. However, someone might rightly ask at this point by what path I have penetrated into such hidden antiquity; therefore, so that this may be clear, I explain the matter. Michael Schatta, an Egyptian Copt and formerly my <term>Amanuensis</term> <note>a literary assistant or copyist</note> in Rome for transcribing Coptic and Arabic texts from the Vatican Library, after he had returned to Egypt, was urged by me among other things that if he should find any hieroglyphic inscriptions, he should see to it that they were drawn, a certain sum of money having been assigned for this purpose; which he indeed performed. Among other hieroglyphic fragments, therefore, of which mention will be made in their proper place, he also sent this Astronomical description of the 48 Images, drawn from the ancient Library of the Monastery of St. Mercurius, and prepared as well as could be done, to fulfill the promise made to me. Since I recognized that this smelled of the lamp of the Ancients <note>meaning it showed signs of late-night, diligent study</note> and was in conformity with hieroglyphic doctrine, I present it in this place as something rare and unseen to the curious Reader...

->### CLASS VII. HIEROGLYPHIC MATHEMATICS 205 CHAPTER VI.<-

I have thought it timely to share this; for although many parts were mutilated and imperfect, through continuous study and diligence it has been brought about that whatever was missing or appeared obscure has been clarified, polished by the file of a <term>Daedalean mind</term> <note>A reference to Daedalus, the mythical craftsman, implying great ingenuity or artistic skill</note> from the very fountain of hieroglyphics. A truly remarkable difference shines forth between these and the spheres of the Greeks. The Egyptians did not place the Equator, but rather the Zodiac at the base; so that the center of each hemisphere represented not the pole of the World, but the pole of the Zodiac. Secondly, the figures sketched with hieroglyphic symbols do not correspond exactly to their locations, but for the most part differ. Nor should this seem strange to anyone, since the Egyptians attempted to express in these hemispheres not so much the stars, but rather the station of the Deities in that vast face of the firmament, as was said above. For they did not think, as the Greeks did, that the figures of the Deities were composed by a cluster of stars; rather, they called a certain gathering of stars the "station" of such-and-such a Deity, whom they believed ruled in such-and-such a place in the sky. For they did not, like those who came after them, ascribe the effects shining forth in the lower World to the hidden influence of the stars, but to the power and efficacy of the Deities established in such-and-such a place in the heavens, as has been said.

<margin>Achilles Tatius</margin> <note>The original text cites "Achilles Statius," likely referring to the 2nd-century author Achilles Tatius, who wrote a commentary on Aratus.</note>
And Achilles Tatius in his *Introduction* near the end testifies to this same thing. I quote his words:

> In the sphere of the Egyptians, there is nothing considered or named as a Dragon... nor a Bear, nor Cepheus; but other shapes of images and names have been established. Nor is it so in the sphere of the Chaldeans. But the Greeks gave these names to the stars from famous heroes so that they might be easily understood and recognized. <note>original Greek: "Ἐν γοῦν τῇ τῶν Αἰγυπτίων σφαίρᾳ... εὔγνωστα." Kircher provides a Latin translation immediately following, which is here rendered into English.</note>

They also made the Zodiac wider than the Greeks did; in its Northern hemisphere, the hieroglyphic figures of the 12 signs of the Zodiac are seen expressed according to the invention of the ancient Astronomy of those still unrefined ages. In the Southern hemisphere, you will find the same figures repeated, but abbreviated: from which it becomes entirely clear from where the characters of the signs used to this day (which they resemble) originated. Nor should the Reader look here for degrees of declination, or latitude of the stars, or similar divisions; since, as I said, that was not the intent of the ancients; rather, they attempted to express the stations of the Gods solely through 12 Rhombs, which they themselves called the <term>twelve-towered fortress</term> <note>original Greek: δωδεκάπυργον (dodekapyrgon)</note>. I wished to deduce all these things here at length, lest the curious Reader remain ignorant of the Egyptians' plan in placing 48 astronomical images upon the sky. And so, to the Rhomb.

Note that the order of the Signs was placed here beginning from **Aries** <note>original: ♈</note>, although the Egyptian <term>Hieromanthae</term> <note>Priest-interpreters of sacred mysteries</note> took their beginning from **Capricorn**; the reason for which we gave in the preceding pages. Hence it seemed fit to mark them with two different sets of numerical figures to avoid confusion.

# CHAPTER VII 208 EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

->*The arrangement of Astronomical Figures according to the mind of the Egyptians, which Michael Schatta the Egyptian extracted from ancient Egyptian monuments and transmitted to the Author.*<-

<image-desc>A partial view of a circular astronomical chart or planisphere on the left side of the page. The chart contains concentric rings with degree markings and symbols of the zodiac, including a scorpion representing Scorpius. Near the center of the diagram, the word "Delta" is written within a triangular region. Various stars and Latin labels are scattered within the chart's sections.</image-desc>

The astrological-hieroglyphic figures placed in the heavens by the Egyptians are 48 in total, as will be made clear in due time in the interpretation of the Barberini Obelisk; by these figures, they promised that fortune to those born during their ascent or culmination which they expressed through symbols. For they report, as I said above, that they arranged certain stations of the Divinities, in which they believed those deities acted by a particular influence upon the lower things committed to their faith and protection; hence they were called by the Egyptians <term>pylones etoi stathmoi</term> <note>original: "πυλῶνες ἤτοι σταθμοί" — gates or stations</note>, stations or mansions of the Gods, because in them they attended to the things committed to them with watchful care. Twelve principal ones among these they arranged in the slant of the Zodiac; the rest they placed partly in the North and partly in the South, as is evident from the two attached hemispheres transmitted to me by Michael Schatta the Egyptian. And indeed, the Greeks and eventually all posterity embraced this number of 48 figures; although, as is clear from the hemispheres, the Egyptians differ from the Greeks in both position and order, with the Greeks substituting their own Divinities in place of the Egyptian ones, and as if honoring them by this celestial <term>chorothesia</term> <note>original: "χοροθεσίᾳ" — arrangement of the dance or regional placement</note>. And concerning the mystical significance of the twelve presidents arranged in the twelve-fold divisions of the Zodiac, we have discoursed amply above in Chapter 3; it remains for us to discuss the rest at an equal pace, beginning with the Northern hemisphere.

<margin>Northern Figures of the Kingdoms of Ammon.</margin>
The first figure of the Kingdom of Ammon, then, after the twelve <term>Oecodespotas</term> <note>original: "Oecodeſpotas" — Lords of the House/Zodiacal rulers</note> of the Zodiac, occurs in the region of Ammon, or the district of Aries: a triangle, which the Egyptians call the **Delta**, and in the Coptic language it denotes the same as a "three-cornered gate," through which the entrance for the Gods into Egypt lies open. This is nothing other than that lower part of Egypt, as was shown in the first volume of the first Treatise, which the Nile, divided by a branching stream at Memphis, once established as having grown from the accumulation of Nilotic mud; it was of such great fertility that they thought it should not undeservedly be called the home of the immortal Gods and the heaven of the Gods. They call it the Gate of the Gods because through it an entrance lies open to an abundance of all good things granted by the liberality and beneficence of the Gods; which the Ibis, a Mercurial animal <note>The Ibis was sacred to Thoth, whom the author identifies with the Roman Mercury</note>, while expressing it with its legs spread apart, simultaneously points out under the protection of which Divinity the **Delta** resides. Hence, in that region of the sky overhanging Egypt, they established a similar triangle or **Delta** composed of three stars, and posterity followed this with the highest cult and veneration as a station of the Mercurial Divinities favoring Egypt, which the Greeks also included among their own constellations. See what we have recited in the first volume, pages 8, 9, 10, 11, in the Pamphilian Obelisk book 3, and in various other places.

II. The second figure is noted as the station of **Nephra**, who, since she has the things of the lower Horizon committed to her faith, undertakes to defend the Nilotic Delta—that is, Egypt, over which she is placed—against all injuries of the nightly chill...

...undertakes. He sits, to indicate power; he holds a whip in his hand, to secretly signify the driving away of evils. He wears a headdress <note>original: "tutulum"</note> composed of sprouts, from which two serpents emerge, to indicate the life and fertility which he confers. He carries a handled cross <note>The *Ankh*, or *Crux Ansata*, a symbol of life</note>, to indicate the abundance of his influence.

III. The Iconism <note>A term used by Kircher to mean a symbolic image or diagram</note> contained in the same district of Ammon; the image of another tutelary deity is placed there with bent knees, and by its very position and the arrangement of its body, it expresses the deity of Ammon (as we have shown elsewhere), as if standing opposite to Ammon.

IV. An Iconism of the Typhonian Dragon (who has placed his station around the North Pole, and is, as it were, the indicator of the Typhonian Kingdom) in a state of supplication.

V. An Iconism is placed within the Rhombus of Apis, subjected to the jurisdiction of the Bull <note>Taurus</note>; it is a Hen with chicks, which the Egyptians worshipped as a Venereal <note>associated with Venus/love</note> deity of fertility. VI. An Iconism, established within the same Rhombus, contains the image of one sitting on a throne, distinguished by a headdress of grain-ears and bovine horns, carrying a Teraphim <note>A cult image or idol</note> in one hand and a handled cross in the other; it is the image of Isis, the tutelary deity of Egypt, the inventor of grain and of agriculture by means of oxen, as the symbols show. The seat is the indicator of power; the Teraphim is the symbol of the Apis-amulet, and the Cross is the symbol of benign influence, as if she were opposing herself to the Typhonian Dragon, which Iconism IV displays. See Volume I, page 185, where ample mention is made of this image. This Iconism corresponds to the Cassiopeia of the Greeks.

VII. An Iconism, established within the Rhombus of the Twins <note>Gemini</note>, is the image of Anubis, conspicuous for his dog's head, who carries an arrow in one hand and a pipe in the other; these are symbols of the Nilotic deity, and signify the excess of drought and heat, which is tempered by the governance of Anubis. See the *Pamphilian Obelisk*.

VIII. An Iconism of Pan is an image in human form carrying a young goat, and bearing a staff in one hand and a serpent in the other. The goat is a symbol of playful fertility, as we proved in the *Pamphilian Obelisk*; the staff is a symbol of power and vigilance; the serpent is a symbol of life. They suggest by this Iconism the care and diligence of the Panic deity, by which he is driven to defend the things committed to his faith against the imminent Typhonian force, which is contrary to the fertility and life of things.

IX. An Iconism within the Rhombus of Hermanubis, which corresponds to the Crab <note>Cancer</note>, is an image distinguished by a headdress, carrying a musical instrument in its hands, in place of which the Greeks put the lyre. It indicates, however, that by the authority and power granted to it by Hermanubis, it reduces the burning heats (which the Typhonian force brings in at this place for the destruction of things) to a harmonic temperament, and undertakes to defend against the hostile force of Typhon.

# CHAPTER VII. THE EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

->The Egyptians call this the *Agathodæmon* <note>original: "Agathodæmona"; a "good spirit" or protective deity often depicted as a serpent</note>; concerning which I have written extensively in the *Pamphilian Obelisk*.<-

XI. The illustration displays the image of the Great Bear, which the Arabs call *Benath alnaaghs* <note>original: "بنات النعش"; meaning "Daughters of the Bier"</note>, that is, the daughters of the funeral bier; the Egyptians call it the *Vehicle of Osiris*. For in this twelfth-part <term>dodecamorio: a 30-degree division of the zodiac</term>, Osiris—that is, the Nile—is imagined to be carried over the land of Egypt as if by a certain vehicle through the force of the inundation, which occurs under the sign of Momphta <note>the Egyptian Leo</note>, in order to animate and fertilize the land alongside his follower, the Ophionian Agathodæmon. You will find all these things explained more fully in the *Pamphilian Obelisk*, Book 8, under the "Sacred Writing of the Lion," and below in the chapter on the 28 mansions of the Moon.

XII. The illustration placed within the Rhombus of Isis (or the Virgin) is a tree, in whose branches a Dog and an Ibis reside on either side, as we have proved above from the Astrology of the Egyptians, which Rabbi Aben Ezra <note>original: "R. Auenar"; referring to the medieval scholar Abraham ibn Ezra</note> translated into the Hebrew language. The tree indeed represents the entire substance of vegetable nature, whose presiding deities are Mercury and Isis; these are aptly denoted by the Dog and the Ibis, as we demonstrated in the *Pamphilian Obelisk*. For when the abundance of Nilotic waters under the twelfth-part of the Ear-bearing Virgin <note>original: "Spicilegæ Virginis"; referring to the star Spica</note>—that is, Isis—gave great hope for a rich harvest and other plants, they consecrated Mercurial deities to this sign as sentinels. This was done lest the seeds conceived in the earth by the moist substance brooding over it should be dried up by Typhonian force <note>referring to Set/Typhon, the god of chaos and drought</note> through a lack of water, or suffocated by an excess. Through their vigilance and care, the rising of the Nile would provide the Egyptian land with the desired benefit against adverse powers.

XIII. The illustration placed within the Rhombus of Ompha (or the Scales) displays a deity with a bovine form <note>original: "βούμορφος"; Greek for "ox-shaped"</note> or transformed with a bull's head, above which hangs a beam in the shape of a plow, as we proved above from Aben Ezra. By these is noted the station of the presiding spirits of spermatic nature. Under the protection of the deity Ompha, who balances all things in equal proportion, nature was promoted and perfected through the industry of the presiding spirits of agriculture (whose symbols were the Ox and the plow), after the land was stripped of its Nilotic covering and broke forth into a rich crop with various sproutings.

XIV. The illustration placed under the sign of Typhon (that is, the Scorpion) was, according to the testimony of Aben Ezra, an image of a naked human figure, holding a torch in one hand and a sting or small spear in the other, and wearing a Raven on its head; this indicated the spirits who are followers of Typhon. By the nakedness, the earth is indicated when stripped of its waters; by the spear, the drying power of the rays is shown, which threatens the destruction of vegetable nature by the withdrawal of necessary moisture (which they also hint at via the torch). By the Raven, however—an animal that feeds on carcasses and carrion—the contagion of venomous animals born from the rot of the earth at this time is aptly denoted. All of these are the effects of Typhon and his followers. See the *Pamphilian Obelisk*.

XV. The illustration placed under the sign of Arueris (or the Archer) is an image in human form, notable for a triple-part headdress, which appears to sacrifice a goat by grasping its horns. By these they indicate nothing other than the station of the spirits of the Typhonian phalanx of "rival-artists" <note>original: "ἀντιτέχνων"; Greek for those who oppose or mimic a craft</note>, whose...

The care is for the kid-goat with its horns cut back; that is, by taming the scorching power of the Sun's rays, the Typhonian <note>Typhon was associated by the Egyptians with chaos and destructive heat</note> fertility is fostered and sustained, with the seed enclosed in the bowels of the earth, to produce a new offspring of vegetable nature. This occurs under this sign, as we have shown above in the interpretation of the Egyptian Zodiac. This image is also found in the Bembine Tablet <note>A famous bronze tablet from antiquity depicting Egyptian deities and symbols, much studied by Kircher</note>, as will be seen in its proper place.

**XVI. and XVII.** The illustration, under the sign of Anubis or Capricorn, shows a standing Dog-headed Ape <term>Cynocephalus; a baboon-headed figure often associated with Thoth or lunar deities</term>, who binds Capricorn with a thong. By this it was aptly indicated that, the fertile nature of Capricorn being bound by Anubis—that is, the power of the Sun being weakened by its low position <note>Referring to the Winter Solstice</note>—the Moon and its attendant Spirits (which they indicated through the Dog-headed Ape) rise up and exercise the substitute power of the Sun. They supply sufficient moisture to nourish and strengthen the seminal substance enclosed within the bowels of the earth. Truly, the **XVIII.** illustration of the Dog marks the station of the Sothiac Deities <note>Related to the star Sirius, or Sothis</note>.

<margin>With a coiled-tail-snake-form <note>original Greek: κυλοτερπουροφιμόρφῳ</note></margin>
**XIX.** The illustration is placed under the Rhombus of Aquarius, and it is the image of a Giant man dressed in the Egyptian fashion, conspicuous for his headdress <note>original: tutulo</note>, because he holds a club in his right hand and the scepter of Mophta <note>A Kircherian term for a creative or demiurgic force</note> in his left. Through the Giant body and the club, he signifies strength over earthly things; through the headdress, he signifies the manifold power which he holds over the air, fire, earth, and the life of things; through the Mophtic scepter, he marks dominion over the substance of moist nature. This he exerts in the Canopic Kingdom while he nourishes, solidifies, strengthens, subdues, and animates the seed enclosed in the earth by rains and snows, preparing it to conceive the various offspring of things. And this is the station which the Egyptians called the "Inclusion of Osiris in the Ark," as was proven in Treatise II from Plutarch, where we also interpreted the symbolic allusions at length.

**XX.** The illustration is placed under the Rhombus of Ichthon <note>The Fishes/Pisces</note>, and it is a female figure, which appears in the Bembine Tablet conspicuous for her veil, sitting and with swollen breasts, carrying in one hand a Lotus-shaped scepter and in the other a Handled Cross <term>Crucem ansatam; the Ankh, symbol of life</term>. Her thigh is also adorned with the same Tautic characters <note>Symbols related to Thoth/Hermes</note>. By the female figure, with swollen breasts and conspicuous veil, they marked the station of the fertile Deities; the seeds of the things of the World are indeed still covered beneath the earth, but now the earth is imbued with the spirit of the Sun and is breaking forth into open germination. This is aptly suggested by the Lotus-bearing scepter and shown by the Handled Crosses with which the thigh is marked. By these, the various mixtures of seminal principles, struck by the arrows of the Solar rays, burst forth into the fertile generation of all things. This happens under this Rhombus of Ichthon, or the station of Pisces: for Ichthon, through his attendants, <margin>* Iamblichus</margin> according to the testimony of Iamblichus, leads the principle of hidden things out of the darkness under which they lay into the light. Thus, those things which the Deities of the preceding sign had hidden away enclosed in the earth, he leads into open and fertile offspring as the earth gradually opens—that is, as the Sun gradually rises and strikes the earth more powerfully with its rays.

We have seen the mystical meanings of the Northern Constellations; it remains for us to open the secrets of the Southern ones with equal pace.

# CHAPTER VII 212 OEDIPUS AEGYPTIACUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

<margin>Southern Images.</margin>
**Image XXI.** In the Southern Kingdom of Osiris, beneath the Rhomb <note>A geometric division of the zodiacal sky</note> of Ammon or the Ram, there appears in the first place a serpent entwined around a staff. This indicates the station of the "Good Spirits" <note>original: *Agathodaemonum*</note>, the guardians of the life of things. These spirits, having entered through the Nilotic Delta—which is to say, the "Gate of the Gods," as we explained above—awaken all things to life under the protection of Ammon. They arrange the beneficial moisture in the farthest reaches of the South at the proper time, which Image XIX aptly suggests through the overflowing waters of the Nile shown above.

**Image XXII.** Under the sign of Apis <note>The sacred bull</note> in the South, they place a statue of Pan; that is, the station of the Panic Deities. Under their protection, all things conspire toward the fertile production of nature, which happens at this time.

**Images XXIII & XXIV.** Positioned under the signs of the Twins <note>Gemini</note> and the Cancer, these show a Serpent-bearer with a spear, above whom towers a ship distinguished by the heads of Rams. In the middle of this ship stands a Bull, or Apis. By the spear-bearing Serpent-bearer, the station of the Arimanian Powers <note>Darker or destructive spiritual forces, often associated with Persian dualism</note> is indicated, by which the moistening power of the solar rays is destroyed by a parching force. Here is placed Apis carried in a ship—that is, Ormuzd <note>original: *Orimazes*, the principle of light/good</note>, the Sun—carried over the Southern region as if through moisture. By the attractive power of his rays, he draws new moisture from the rivers, lakes, and seas; when these are resolved into rains, the new preludes to the rising of the Nile are prepared.

**Images XXV & XXVI.** Positioned under the Rhomb of Cancer and the Lion, this is Anubis piercing a wolf or a Typhonian wild beast. By this, they wished to indicate the station of the Mercurial or Nilotic Deities, whose care it is to accelerate the rising of the Nile at this time. This occurs during the rising of the Dog Star <note>original: *Canicula*</note>, which in Egyptian is <unclear>☿</unclear> or Sothis; we have shown on the Pamphilian Obelisk that Mercury was also called by this name. At this time, the earthy and parching power of Typhon—appropriately indicated by the wolf, a fierce land animal into which Typhon is said to have transformed himself—is destroyed by the abundance of the Nilotic moisture.

**Images XXVII, XXVIII, XXIX, & XXX.** These are positioned under the signs of the Virgin and the Balance <note>Libra</note>. First is the Giant <note>original: *Gygas*</note>, whom the Greeks call Orion; he is joined by an Owl and a Quail, according to Ibn Ezra <note>original: *Auenar*</note>, which are symbols of ill omen. By the Giant, an inauspicious "Titanic" station is forenoted—that is, a station of spirits who suffocate all things by an excess of moisture. Opposed to their tyranny is a Lion carried in a ship—that is, Momphta and Omphta <note>Kircher's terms for Egyptian generative powers</note>. The former, with his followers, seeks to bless the earth with sufficient moisture, while the latter strives to temper the excess of suffocating moisture brought on immoderately by the Titanic force, reducing it to a middle state. See what we have discussed copiously on these matters in the interpretation of the Bembine Tablet <note>A famous bronze tablet with Egyptianizing motifs, central to Kircher's theories</note>.

**Image XXXI.** Positioned under the southern Rhomb of the Scorpion, this shows a Crocodile, an argument for the Typhonian tyranny. It is a hostile station because the opposing spirits, who were unable to destroy the good through an excess of moisture, now attempt to finish it through a lack of the same, the Nile having now receded within its banks and the land increasing. It is called the station of Suchus—that is, the Crocodile—into which the Egyptians report Typhon was transformed.

# CLASS VII. HIEROGLYPHIC MATHEMATICS 213 CHAPTER VII

Illustrations XXXII and XXXIII, positioned beneath the southern Rhombs <note>Rhomb refers here to a diamond-shaped division of the celestial map</note> of Sagittarius and Capricorn, contain the image of a human figure piercing a Hippopotamus with one hand, while with the other he points to an Ibis devouring a Serpent. By the man of youthful appearance, distinguished by a headband, Horus is understood; by the Hippopotamus, Typhon is meant. Horus is indeed the symbol of the reborn World, by whom the contagious power of the remaining moisture is pierced through. These things are also indicated by the Ibis, the symbol of the Mercurial Spirits <note>original: "Mercurialium Geniorum"; referring to spirits associated with Thoth/Hermes/Mercury</note>, by whose help the swarming multitude of harmful things, born from the putrefaction of the earth, is consumed at this time.

Illustrations XXXIV, XXXV, and XXXVI, contained under the southern Rhomb of Aquarius and Pisces, are *the Nile*, *the Hydra*, and the high *Altar*; by these, the stations of the three Nilotic Spirits—guardians of the southern waters and preservers of the fiery nature—are expressed. The first activate the moisture enclosed in the bowels of the earth; the second make the same fertile; the third administer the subterranean heat by which things are fertilized. These are aptly expressed through *the Nile*, *the Hydra*, and the *Altar* furnished with fire. But concerning these matters, a copious amount of material for discussion will be given in due time in the interpretation of the *Barberini Obelisk*.

Reader, take note that only the figures, and those quite imperfect, were sent by the previously cited *Michael Schatta*. However, as much as I could gather from his letters written to me in *Arabic*, I have restored them to the correct Egyptian meaning and divided them into certain stations of the Gods, so that the intention of the Egyptians in establishing them might appear more clearly. But all these things, as I said, will be better revealed in the interpretation of the *Barberini Obelisk*.

<margin>The impious superstition and divination of the Egyptians and Chaldeans based on the illustrations of the 48 stars.</margin>
You have, therefore, the arrangement of the 48 Illustrations placed in the heavens by the Egyptians, and their physical interpretations, which they also adapted according to a certain analogy to archetypal and moral principles. Thus, through the symbols of said Illustrations, the intellectual World might be understood. In this world, they subtly suggested the duties distributed to each choir of Spirits <note>original: "Geniorum"</note>, and the effects they imprint both in the triple series of Worlds and, most especially, in the spheres of souls; for from these they deduced the order of fates. From the rising of these Illustrations of Spirits, they believed they could know an infallible conjecture regarding the fortune or fate of anyone's Birth. Hence, they strove anxiously to appease each of these stations of the Gods as soon as they emerged from the Horizon or culminated in their ascent, whether by sacrifices or by rites and ceremonies. For just as they believed that all the misery and calamity of the Newborn depended on the adverse ascent of Spirits, so they promised themselves fortune and happiness from the benevolent and propitious ascent of the Good Spirits <note>original: "Agathodæmonum"; from the Greek 'Agathodaemon' meaning a good spirit or protective deity</note>. Hence, they strove to appease the former with sacrifices so they would not harm, and to attract the latter with appropriate things and sacrifices so they would be of benefit. Since, however, the seven principal Deities of the planets <note>original: "planetarum Numina"</note> are continually joined—now good with good, now good with malignant, and then malignant with malignant—they pronounced judgments on prosperous or adverse outcomes of affairs according to the ratio of the prosperous or adverse conjunction. See what we have discussed more at length on these matters above in Chapters 3, 4, and 5.

# CHAPTER VII. OF THE EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

This entire collection of <term>Asterisms</term><note>Groups of stars or constellations</note> possessed four principal Deities, by whose influential power both the series of linked <term>Genii</term><note>Guardian spirits or intermediary beings connecting the divine to the earthly</note> and the economy of the lower world are governed. This fourfold group of Genii was called by the Egyptians the "heads of the fourfold mundane chain," while the Greeks named it the "Fourfold Divine Nature" <note>original: τὴν Θειῶν τεξαπλόα</note>. Indeed, the Egyptians adorned this tetrad with those symbols which you will see marked in the illustration of the following Section—representing the cycles of Egyptian years—encircled by a Serpent. The Greeks, however, displayed their "Fourfold of the Gods" <note>tetractys</note> in exactly the manner shown in the subjoined figure, which we have drawn from a Gem communicated to me by Peter Stephanonius, a man most skilled in Antiquity. ## DIGRESSION.

### *Whether the Heaven is a certain Book; and whether various combinations of stars compose a kind of writing, in which future events may be read, inscribed by the finger of God.*

<margin>The Hebrews and Arabs assert that heaven is a book in which future events are read.</margin>
I find that the Hebrews and Arabs were the first assertors of this dogma. For when they beheld the Heaven marked by the Egyptians and Greeks with such strange and unusual images of false Deities, they were driven—both by the unsuitability of the thing and by the prohibition of their law—to architect another dogma, constituted from celestial characters. For these people, partly because they believed fatal laws were described in heaven, and partly because they were misled by the testimonies of the most ancient Authors, judged it to be by no means vain or idle that the heavens exerted themselves upon the lower World with such unusual effects. They arrived at the opinion that the expanse of the firmament is nothing other than a certain book, marked with stars as if with certain letters, from whose harmonious combination the events of all ages and the decrees of men might be read, inscribed by the finger of God. But so that they may more skillfully defend this foolish fabrication, they prove it from sacred texts, which they ridiculously twist to stabilize their own opinions, depraving them in marvelous ways against reason. They allege, therefore, first that passage from Isaiah 34:
<margin>The foolish interpretation of Scripture by Hebrew Astrologers.</margin>
-> And the heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll: <-
<note>original Hebrew: ונגלו כספר השמים</note>
*And the heavens shall be rolled up like a book.* Which they explain thus: *And the heavens shall be rolled up like a book, exhibiting the accounts of all present, past, and future events.* They confirm this passage from the 1st verse of Genesis:
-> In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth: <-
<note>original Hebrew: בראשית ברא אלהים את השמים ואת הארץ</note>
Which words they wrongly interpret in this fashion: *In the beginning God created the letters or the writing of heaven;* where they explain the particle *et* <note>the Hebrew particle 'eth' (את)</note> as the letters or writing of heaven. This is an entirely incongruous exposition, deceitfully contorted to persuade the unskilled of that superstitious celestial writing. For who among the Commentators of Holy Scripture has ever interpreted this particle as anything other than the accusative case marker? Which is also manifest...
<meta>The text cuts off as it prepares to further debunk the grammatical claims of the astrologers.</meta>

# CHAPTER VII. 216 EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

<note>The author is Athanasius Kircher, a 17th-century Jesuit polymath. Here he argues against the idea that the sky is a literal book of letters.</note>

This is clear from the following phrase: *et hashamayim ve'et ha'aretz* <note>original: "את השמים ואת הארץ" — Genesis 1:1, "the heavens and the earth"</note>, (which those who are consciously defending a bad cause studiously keep silent) where the same particle is repeated; in place of which, the Chaldean paraphrase <note>The Targum, an ancient Aramaic translation of the Hebrew Bible</note> uses *Yath* <note>original: "ית"</note>, an article commonly used by the Chaldeans to form the accusative case. According to the opinion of these people, therefore, the first verse of Genesis ought to be read: *In the beginning God created the letter of heaven, and the letter of the earth*; an interpretation so dull and foolish that nothing more absurd could be imagined. In the same way, they read that passage from the same book of Genesis, *and they shall be for signs* <note>original: "והיו לאתת" — Genesis 1:14</note>, as *and they shall be for letters*; a truly reckless audacity. Nor do they stop here in their attempt to achieve their aim. In that passage of Psalm 17 <note>Psalm 19 in modern numbering</note>, *Their sound has gone out into all the earth*, they interpret the word *Kolam* <note>their voice</note> as *Kavam* <note>their line</note>, meaning "their lines," that is, the lines of a script; an equally poor and clumsy exposition, no better than the first.

<margin>
Authors of the impious opinion asserting that heaven is a book in which future events are described by the finger of God.
</margin>

Having laid these worm-eaten foundations, they say that the heaven or *Rakia* <note>The Hebrew term for the firmament or expanse</note>—that expanse, I say—is like a certain parchment skin, in which the stars represent letters and the constellations represent words of future events engraved by the finger of God, according to the verse: *The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaims the work of his hands.* In this, they say, all the successes of future things, the changes of kingdoms and lower affairs, as well as the entire lot and fortune of private men, are set forth as if through a book intelligible only to the Wise. And they say the propagators of this opinion were first [Simeon bar] Yochai, who explains it in the *Zohar*, Akiba the author of the *Book of Formation* <note>Sefer Yetzirah</note>, Maimonides <note>Rambam</note>, Abraham ibn Daud, Abraham ibn Ezra, David Kimhi <note>Radak</note>, Yom Tov, Levi ben Gershon <note>Ralbag</note>, Isaac Abarbanel, and countless others; whom some Latin writers, more superstitious than the rest, have followed. They strive to establish their dogma from a certain apocryphal book entitled the *Narrative of Joseph*, which they claim Origen cites in his book *Whether the Stars Act*; in which these words are found: *I read in the tablets of heaven what will happen to you and your sons.* To this they also twist that passage of St. Augustine in Book 2 *Against the Manichaeans*, chapter 21: *Nor should it be believed that thoughts can lie hidden in those celestial bodies as they lie hidden in these [human] bodies; but just as certain movements of the mind appear in the face, and especially in the eyes, so in that clarity and simplicity of the celestial bodies I do not think any movements of the mind are hidden at all.* Yet there, no mention is made of "celestial writing," but the Holy Doctor only establishes a certain comparison of the celestial face to the human face. Nor does that line of Orpheus favor them: *Your certain order runs in the stars by immutable commands* <note>original Greek: "Σὺ μὲν ἐπ' ἄστροις τάξις ἀναλλάκτως ἐφ' ὁμοιώσει τέχνα"</note>. For while they drag this quote into their argument, they are clearly convicted of vanity; since anyone who considers the context of the Orphic hymns more scrupulously will find that it speaks not of celestial writing, nor of the character-letters with which they disfigure heaven, but of the immutable necessity of nature shining forth most powerfully in the heavens.

Cornelius Agrippa.
Paracelsus.
Robert Fludd.
</margin>

# CLASS VII. HIEROGLYPHIC MATHEMATICS. CHAPTER VII

<margin>Postel <note>Guillaume Postel (1510–1581), a French linguist and mystic.</note></margin>
Points form lines, surfaces are made from lines, and bodies from surfaces; truly, to those whom God has granted the knowledge of such secret languages, writings, and hidden characters, it will also be given to read—as if with illuminated eyes—the true natures of things, the movements and alterations of the stars, and all other operations and executions, and to understand them through reading. Postel subscribes to this view, who in his *Commentary on the Sefer Yetzirah* <note>The "Book of Formation," a primary text of Jewish mysticism</note> vainly, not to say foolishly, claims knowledge of this celestial writing for himself in these words: "If I were to say that I have seen in heaven, in the very characters of the sacred language first beautifully set forth by Ezra, all those things which are established in the nature of things—as I saw them not explicitly, but implicitly—scarcely anyone would believe me; yet God and his Christ are my witnesses that I do not lie." You said it correctly: "scarcely anyone would believe me," since those who know your temperament might deservedly doubt your words. It is clear from the following words that Postel certainly drew all this knowledge from the superstitious doctrine of the Arabs, of which he was a most diligent student: "The stars," he says, "are finally outlined and shaded with their lines by divine fire expressed in the waters of heaven; they are sacred characters, expressed in the heavens with such power that the truth of future events can even be obtained. A trace of this science still exists in Jericho and many other cities of the Ishmaelites <note>A term used here for Arabs/Muslims</note>, although the figures of the sacred script are greatly depraved and corrupted."

<margin>The writing which the stars are believed to display is thought to be Hebrew.</margin>
And so the authors cited just before feel that the stars display a certain celestial writing. Now we must see with which characters it is composed, and how its reading should be established. As for the first point, a certain modern author named Gaffarel <note>Jacques Gaffarel (1601–1681), a French scholar and astrologer</note> thinks he unravels this difficulty in the book which he titled in French *Les Curiositez inouyes*, that is, *Unheard-of Curiosities*. He concludes, following the mind of both the Rabbis and other authors of this opinion, that this writing can be none other than Hebrew, even though the Arabs wish it to be nothing but their own, that is, Arabic. Postel acts as the decider of the dispute; suppressing the vanity and presumption of the most cunning Arabs, he subscribes to the cause of the Hebrews, which Gaffarel describes at length and through various examples in the cited French book, as will be seen shortly. The alphabet brought forward by Gaffarel, extracted from the *Hebrew Grammar* of Abraham de Balmes <note>A 15th-century Italian-Jewish physician and translator</note>, which he calls "celestial," is that which follows, in which the black points are said to represent the stars.

These letters of the Alphabet serve the asterisms <note>groups of stars or constellations</note> of both hemispheres in such a way that individual asterisms, constructed from said letters, might exhibit something—either good or evil—to one skilled in reading these characters. I have seen fit to include both characteristic hemispheres in this place, so that the Reader might recognize, as if from a certain prototype, how many trifles human curiosity entangles itself in through useless effort, and from the display of a business so slippery, utterly arbitrary, and resting on no foundation. For it is so uncertain, inconsistent, and disordered <note>original Greek: ἄτακτον (atakton)</note>, that although I have applied myself with the greatest zeal and industry to the comparison of said characters with Astronomical asterisms, I have not been able to find even one that refers to the commonly known asterisms even by conjecture; therefore, I have judged it a thing to be utterly rejected as a useless and fanatical invention. Furthermore, to properly complete the reading of this writing, there are difficulties of immense doubt which seem impossible to overcome by any reasoning. For if a reading is to be established, I ask: where should the first beginning of the reading be made? For besides

Since it can be defined by no reason why good or evil should be portended to this region, city, or man rather than that one, or at what time the threatening writing is to be fulfilled. Gaffarel <note>Jacques Gaffarel, a French scholar and astrologer</note> responds to this, citing Rabbi Abiudam: *“To know how to perfectly understand this celestial writing, one must exactly note the vertical stars; for those which are over a Kingdom usually show what must happen to it.”* <note>original French: "Pour sçauoir parfaictement entendre ceſte eſcriturę celeſte, il faut exactement remarquer les eſtoilles verticales; car celles qui ſont ſur vn Royaume, monſtrent ordinairement ce qui luy doit arriver."</note> That is: *“To know the perfect account of this celestial writing, it is necessary to exactly note the stars vertical to any Kingdom, for these ordinarily show whatever ought to happen to it.”* But on the contrary: since the stars

Yet experience teaches that the *perioeci* have a great variety of effects: some are pressed by wars, famine, and other calamities, while others enjoy the perpetual happiness of peace. # CLASS VII. HIEROGLYPHIC MATHEMATICS 221 CHAPTER VII

...placed first in the middle, and finally at the end of some notable asterism <note>A grouping of stars, smaller than a constellation</note>, the meaning of those things which they indicate may be elicited. Gaffarel <note>Jacques Gaffarel (1601–1681), a French scholar and astrologer who claimed the stars formed Hebrew letters</note> explains the matter with an example; in this French word *AME* <note>Soul</note>, he says, if *F* is joined to it at the beginning, you create the word *FAME* <note>Hunger/Reputation</note>; if *R* is joined to the middle of the same, it creates the word *ARME* <note>Weapon</note>, and so on for the rest. He adds that since there are stars of various magnitudes in the asterisms, the larger ones act like capital letters and are more significant, and therefore sometimes one must attend to them alone. Thus (he says) if in this word, *EMPEREUR* <note>Emperor</note>, I want to read the word *PERE* <note>Father</note>, I would write the word *EMPEREUR* like this: emPEREur; and thus the capital letters alone signify *PERE*. Similarly, if in the word *ROYAUME* <note>Kingdom</note>, I want to read the word *ROME*, I would write *ROyauME*.

<margin>Refutation</margin> But who would not laugh at this childish and most inept way of philosophizing? For if the planets, comets, and other new stellar phenomena produce this change of meaning in the celestial scripture; I ask that they show me what letter those solitary stars constitute, since a single star is incapable of forming any letter, but many stars, as they freely admit, are necessary to form a shape. Perhaps they will respond that this happens in great conjunctions, where a gathering of planets occurs. But let us suppose they form a square; who then could discern whether that square forms an *Aleph* **א**, or a *Beth* **ב**, or a *He* **ה**, or a *Cheth* **ח**, or a *Mem* **מ**, or any similar letter of square form? For that square which the planets form with the stars could fit all the said letters, as appears in the following letters: **ח ח כ א** <note>Hebrew letters Cheth, Cheth, Kaph, and Aleph, shown here to demonstrate their similar blocky shapes</note>: in which, since the mere drawing of lines alone designates the shapes of the letters, the placement of stars into a square seems useless and utterly idle. The same must be said of "linear" letters, which consist of only two stars, such as **ן ו ז י** <note>Nun, Vau, Zayin, Yod</note>; and of "triangular" letters, which are mostly formed by three stars, such as **ד ל ט מ ג** <note>Daleth, Lamed, Teth, Mem, Gimel</note> etc.

But the supreme vanity of this "scripture" can be seen no better than through examples. Gaffarel brings forward the following examples from Rabbi Ghomer: first, the head of Medusa, whose five principal and vertical stars portended the ultimate desolation of Greece, while they formed this Hebrew word **חרב**, *Charab* <note>original: "חרב", transliterated as Charab</note>, that is, *desolated*.

<margin>The vanity of the celestial Alphabet is shown through examples.</margin> Truly, he who examines these things more carefully will find nothing but open imposture lurking beneath them; which we show thus. The five principal stars are designated by five white dots imprinted on the letters; where the first letter **ח** (*Cheth*) consists of two stars, **ר** (*Resch*) of one, and the third **ב** (*Beth*) likewise consists of two stars. But as is evident from the "Celestial Alphabet," the letters **ע צ ם ו** <note>Ayin, Tsade, Mem, Vau</note> have exactly the same stellar placement as the first letter of the said word, **ח** (*Cheth*); the second letter **ר** (*Resch*) has the same as **ו** (*Vau*), **ק** (*Koph*), **ד** (*Daleth*); and finally the third has the same as the letters **ת נ כ נ ב** <note>Tav, Nun, Kaph, Nun, Beth</note>. From which it follows that from the said constellation, one can gather not only the word **חרב** (*Charab*), that is, *desolated*, but also all the following words: **כות, סוף, זית, צופ, וקן, חרץ, חרף, ערב, טוב,** <note>A list of Hebrew words that could theoretically be formed using the same star patterns, undermining the specificity of the "prophecy"</note>

of which the first, *tob* <note>original: "טוב"</note>, sounds the same as *good*, and its sense is entirely contrary to the former; the second, *ra* <note>original: "רע"</note>, is the same as *to pledge, to mix, a crow, or a willow*; the third, *charaph* <note>original: "חרף"</note>, the same as *to reproach* or *winter*; the fourth, *kotz* <note>original: "קוץ"</note>, the same as *to move, to disturb, etc.*; the fifth, *zaken* <note>original: "זקן"</note>, the same as *to grow old* or *a beard*; the sixth, *puph* <note>original: "פוף"</note>, the same as *to swim, to fly away,* or *a honeycomb*; the seventh, *shemen* <note>original: "שמן"</note>, the same as *olive* or *oil*; the eighth, *soph* <note>original: "סוף"</note>, the same as *boundary, end,* or *to fail*; the ninth, *tum* <note>original: "טום"</note>, signifies the same as *a covering*, as will be clear from a Hebrew Lexicon. Since, therefore, one and the same interpretation can be fashioned in so many and such varied ways—involving senses now good, now evil—who will ever be assured of the truth of the meaning? It is evident, then, that the said scripture is utterly triffling, and no reason can be devised that might satisfy it in any way.

<margin>Objection 2 against the Celestial Alphabet.</margin>
The second difficulty consists in this: that it cannot be known to which region in particular such misfortunes are portended. But, lest they seem to have said nothing even on this point, they turn to Kabbalistic devices; for from the numbers of a word—for example, *chereb* <note>meaning "sword" or "destruction"</note>—they seek, with greatest but useless labor, the word of some region containing the same number. Such a word, they say, is *Iuan* <note>original: "יון"</note>, that is, *Greece*; and so they divine that the desolation of Greece is imminent because this contains the same number as the word *chereb*, namely 12. But this method of <term>isopsephy</term> <note>The practice of adding up the number values of letters in a word to find connections with other words of the same value; similar to Gematria.</note> is the worst of all, being foolishly and violently distorted to suit their purpose. For when they saw they would not achieve their intent, they assigned different numbers to certain letters than the common School of Arithmeticians assigns to them. Thus for the letter *Resh* <note>ר</note>, which usually signifies 200, they assign 2, having rejected the zeros. In like manner for *Yod* <note>י</note>, which signifies 10, they assign 1, having rejected the zero. But if *Aleph* <note>א</note> should occur, which signifies 1, how will they distinguish this from the unit of *Yod*? I see that they are stuck and can answer nothing, except to openly expose themselves as exceptional impostors to everyone.

<margin>The vanity and falsehood of the Celestial Alphabet is further argued.</margin>
He adduces more such stupid and insane mental tricks from the Rabbis Chomer, Kapol, and Abiudan. When Nabuzardan, he says, was destroying the temple of Jerusalem, the stars directly above it formed these five letters: *netakahu* <note>original: "נתקהו"</note>, which is the same as *to lay waste, to cut off, to lead to ultimate ruin*. They say the letters of this word, resolved by <term>isopsephy</term>, produce the same number as the years the temple lasted from its building until that time. Again, before the Jews saw their scepter shaken and found their liberty captive in Babylon, five stars exhibited these mystical letters: *natak* <note>original: "נתק"</note>, which is the same as *to break, to demolish, to exterminate*;

In like manner, the Persians and Assyrians, after the overthrow of the Monarchies of Kingdoms and Empires, read in four stars directly above—

They say that this word **רוב** <note>original: *rov*, meaning "to strive" or "contend"</note> signifies to litigate, and constitutes the number 208, which is the same as the number of years this Monarchy <note>The Persian Empire</note> lasted, having been established by Cyrus. The end of Greece was shown in a similar way through four stars which composed the word **פרד** <note>original: *parad*, meaning "to divide"</note>, that is, to divide; the number of which, 284, agrees with the duration of this Monarchy. Again, the Monarchy of the Athenians lasted 490 years, a duration shown by three letters of four stars contained under the word **צרר** <note>original: *tsarar*, meaning "to be distressed" or "bound up"</note>, which signifies to be afflicted by narrow straits. With these four stars, four others appear arranged in the form of **ככ** <note>Two Hebrew letters 'Caph'</note>, which they call fatal and mournful letters; but Rabbi Chomer says that by the double Caph, Cecrops and Codrus are signified, under whom this most powerful Kingdom was both begun and consumed. With such trifles do the wits of idle men delight themselves. Furthermore, they say that the Roman Consulate could not extend its power beyond 501 years, because that fatal volume of the heavens had decreed it so, and not otherwise, through 8 stars which composed this word **ראש** <note>original: *rosh*, meaning "head" or "summit"</note>, which signifies head and peak, and contains the number 501: the length of time, clearly, that the dominion of the Roman Consuls lasted. Again, the Monarchy of Julius Caesar, founded to overwhelm the Roman Consulate, lasted almost as many years, indicated by six stars which composed this word **שבר** <note>original: *shavar*, meaning "to break" or "shatter"</note>, which is the same as to break or rupture, and has the number 502. Finally, Rabbi Chomer thinks he has found the approaching end of the Ottoman Empire through the reading of the stars in this manner: today, seven stars are vertical to it and constitute the word **נאה** <note>original: *na'ah*, interpreted here as "to be broken"</note>, which signifies to be weakened, shattered, and afflicted with great pain; and indeed the number of the duration of the said Empire is indicated by the number hidden under the word **נאה**, namely 1025. Therefore, when this year is completed, it is necessary for this dominion and Monarchy to reach its end; which ought to happen in 1655. For by subtracting from the current year of Christ the 630 years in which the Muhammadan perfidy began after Christ, there remains 1025 as the duration of the Ottoman Kingdom.

But it is evident that this whole thing was deceitfully fabricated with great effort, because the word **נאה** does not contain the number 1025, which Chomer—whoever that <term>Rabbinaster</term> <note>A derogatory term for a petty or false Rabbi</note> may be—so anxiously twists to fit his commentary; rather, its number by <term>isopsephy</term> <note>The practice of adding up the number values of letters in a word to find a sum</note> is closer to 26, as will be clear to anyone resolving it according to the art. Nor is it valid to take the letter Aleph (א) for a thousand, as this is a most absurd license and not to be tolerated by any reason; for Aleph is never taken for the number one thousand unless it is marked with a dot. It is clear, therefore, that in all these trifles there is manifest imposture; while they act against the laws of letter-numbers prescribed by the ancients, they now change them, now adding or taking away, so corrupting them that they can scarcely be recognized anymore. Thus, in order to arrive at a hidden goal under a certain sum of numbers that might mark the duration of some Kingdom, they are accustomed to use this shameless license in the responses of numbers, arranging and combining <term>isopsephy</term> <note>original: *τὴν ἰσοψηφίαν*</note> without any scruple.
