It should be noted moreover that the characters of the Planets, as we have said in *Astrology*, were first invented by Hermes and drawn from this Hermetic character-set. For anyone who looks into the matter more deeply will see that all those said characters of the Planets are composed of the Sun, the Moon, the Elements (that is, the Cross), and from the horns of the Ram or Ammon. Thus, the character of ♄ Saturn consists of the cross and one horn of the Ram; the character of ♃ Jupiter is composed of the cross and the other horn of the Ram; ☿ Mercury from the cross, the circle, and the semicircle—that is, from the ☉, ☾, and the Elemental character. The character of Mars is composed of the circle, a straight line, and the figure of the Ram in this way: ♂. The character of Venus from the circle and the cross, as is evident here: ♀. Just as Mercury is the messenger of all the Planets, so he is honored with the insignia of all, as appears in ☿; by which it is secretly hinted that the seeds of all metals lie hidden in Mercury. His purest spirit is so powerful that, in the purest earth prepared chemically, he converts these four similar and <term>geogamic</term> <note>Earth-born or earth-marrying; referring to the relationship between celestial influences and terrestrial matter.</note> natures—♄, ♃, ♀, ♂—into <unclear>indes</unclear> and reduces them into one, as the <term>hieroglyphic</term> <note>Here used to mean a sacred or symbolic diagram.</note> demonstrates. Truly, the character of Mars, fused from the characters of the Sun and the Ram, and that of Venus, fused from the characters of the Sun and the Elements, look toward the Solar work and the process of <term>re-kindling</term> <note>original: "ἀναζωπυρήσεως" (anazopyreseos). A Greek term for the rekindling of a fire or the restoration of life/energy.</note>; in the progress of which that second Mercury finally becomes conspicuous—the uterine brother of the first—once the Lunar and Solar magic of the Elements is complete. This is the most celebrated "Mercury of the Philosophers," whose soul binds and fixes not only the Moon, Jupiter, Mercury, and Venus, but also Mars with indissoluble bonds, and finally, after various revolutions made around the metallic earth, exhibits to us the longed-for Sun of the Philosophers. You see, therefore, how the said Mercury first actuates Saturn, then Jupiter, thirdly the Moon, and afterwards Mars and Venus, and finally exhibits the Sun, according to certain wondrous steps, the septenary number being completed, as the character beautifully denotes. But all these things will later be found more clearly in practice; so that henceforth this whole mystery, proceeding from the Sun and Moon, may be revealed more clearly than the midday light. Hence Hermes, as found in the writings of Haled the Arab <note>Khalid ibn Yazid, an early Umayyad prince and legendary alchemist.</note> cited above, says:

> The Sun is its father, the Moon its mother, and it receives nourishment from the earth, fostered by the Solar and Lunar rays.

We have known from the most ancient astronomers even to our own times, that the Moon is exalted in Taurus, and the Sun in Aries. How aptly these suit "lower astrology" <note>Alchemical astrology or the study of terrestrial correspondences.</note> is demonstrated by the <term>Hermetic characterism</term> with this mark ♉, which is the <term>exaltation</term> <note>The zodiac sign where a planet's influence is most powerful.</note> of the Moon in Taurus, and of the Sun in Aries, as this analysis shows. For the Sun in Aries, a fiery sign, receives its Martian strength after various operations, and as if in its own house, its exaltation from Mars, as the character of Mars ♂ hints; so that the exaltation of the Moon and Sun from ♄, ♃, ☿, and this one from ♂ and ♀, by means of the science of the Elements, may obtain their perfection. The cross itself indicates the mode of proceeding. The Hermetic Character inverted.

Another mystery lies hidden beneath the Hermetic character. For if it is considered inverted, first the horns of Aries appear, which together with the Cross constitute the characters of ♄ Saturn, ♃ Jupiter, and ♂ Mars; then ascending, the Cross serves Venus ♀ and Mercury ☿; finally, the Sun and Moon follow at the bottom. By these they wished to indicate nothing other than the Hermetic triad <note>Latin: ternarium</note> lurking in the monad <note>The "Monad" refers to a single, indivisible unit representing the source of all things</note>; from which it first goes out into certain separate and unknown Saturnine, Martial, and Jovial essences, so that finally the Sun and Moon—which is the goal—may be obtained. For from the Cross comes one, and from two again comes one; in the Cross is the monad, the dyad, the triad, and the decad <note>The numbers 1, 2, 3, and 10</note>, all of which we shall explain: how they are to be understood and what they signify in the Chemical art.

<margin>The elemental world made according to the Archetype.</margin>
Note, therefore, that all things in the World were made according to the Archetypal World; in which the Father generates the Son (the Monad generates the dyad), from which the procession of the one Holy Spirit gives the triad; yet this triad necessarily has the tetrad <note>the number four</note> implied within it. Thus there is the Father considered abstractly according to his divine essence; then the Father as he relates to the Son; and finally the Holy Spirit as he relates to both. There are, therefore, the Father, the Father and Son, and the Holy Spirit. In this way the World was also created. You have four Elements, you have four luminaries—two superior and two inferior, two celestial and two central—by which all things that are created are encompassed. One is not created from one, for this is the property of God alone; it is the part of man to produce one from two.

<margin>The vegetable and mineral kingdoms in the elemental world.</margin>
In the Elemental World there are two kingdoms: the vegetable and the mineral. The latter can subsist by itself, even if there were no man, tree, or herb in the world; the former likewise can endure even if there were no metal or animal in the world. These two were created from one and through one; but a third has life from these two, and exhibits an essence more excellent than them, even though it cannot exist without them and rules over them; because in a triad all virtue is always perfected, but in a dyad or binary it is multiplied. I explain my meaning: In the vegetable kingdom, the "first matter" <note>term: materia prima; the raw, unrefined base substance</note> is the herb or tree, speaking Philosophically, which nature does not allow to go astray, as it is the work of nature alone. In this kingdom, the "second matter" is the seed, and in this the herb or tree is multiplied, and the process goes from the monad into the dyad, and from there into the triad. In the mineral kingdom, metal does not know how to go astray, as nature has reserved its power for itself alone; yet it has a seed, by which the Craftsman works toward multiplication. There is water lurking in the center of their heart, whose digestive faculty is fire; its receptacle or matrix is

For a better understanding of things, so that it may be understood how metals can be compelled to emit and receive seed, it must be noted that the inferior planets <note>The metals on Earth</note> and the superior or celestial planets behave in exactly the same way and proportion; in which, just as the superior planets flow into the inferior ones and not the other way around, so it happens with the inferior planets. Among the planets, you see that Saturn is the highest, followed by Jupiter and Mars; in the middle is the Sun, followed by Venus, Mercury, and the Moon. Therefore, just as Venus does not flow into Mars, but on the contrary Mars flows into Venus; so Mars is not made from Venus, but on the contrary Venus is made from Mars. In this way, Jupiter is also easily converted into Mercury, for Jupiter is second from the firmament, while Mercury is second from the earth, as is evident in the margin, and so on for the others. Just as the Sun occupies the middle place, so it mixes with all things, yet on this condition: that it is never rendered better or more excellent by the inferior ones; so that the superior ones are always connected with the inferior ones by the greater laws of sympathy and friendship. And the closer they are to the Sun, and the more equally they are distant from it—such as Mars and Venus, Jupiter and Mercury, Saturn and the Moon—the more easily they coalesce in a union. Hence some people, from similar things and without any operation of the Sun (as they think), convert Mars into Venus, Jupiter into Mercury, and Saturn into the Moon; although nothing in operations of this kind, if we weigh the matter in a deeper balance, can be rightly accomplished without the aid of the Sun, which administers its own nature to all metals.

<margin>The character ♀ arises from the character ♈.</margin>
How these things are drawn out by a wonderful reasoning from our Hermetic Caduceus <note>The staff of Hermes/Mercury, a symbol of alchemy</note> is clearly evident. For if the sign of ♈ Aries, consisting of two semicircles, is joined into one circle, the character of Venus ♀ will be born, which nevertheless does not reach the size of the Solar character. By this, indeed, a double degree of the Moon is secretly indicated, or the living Moon existing within, to be handled through the ministry of the Elements, having the power to represent the Solar fullness with its semicircles joined together by art at the same time. If this should happen, it is not to be judged that it has reached the Solar degree by its own nature, but that it is a manufactured work, and cannot reflect the Solar magnitude, inasmuch as its parts are loose, flowing, and dissolved, not solidly compacted into the Solar form.

Whence it is clear from this mystery, that from the character ♈ or ♀, we must not hope for the Sun ☉, since even the ☽ Moon was not originally in the nature of the ✝ cross <note>original: "in natura ✝"; likely referring to the elemental cross or the crucible</note>; yet there lies hidden beneath it, as if under different members, a certain wonderful sympathy, and a certain magnetic force, and a longing for union, by which it easily attracts to itself whatever is sympathetic in the execution of the work; for which the most suitable vessels are required; the form and figure of which our hieroglyphic character itself beautifully demonstrates, from whose symmetry the following figures are born. The Ancients of the Egyptians exhibited this entire craftsmanship through another hierogram <note>a sacred symbolic drawing</note>, and it is that which follows; in which the Beetle <note>the Scarab</note> denotes the primary matter of the metallic art, involving the bodies of the whole World, from which it rolls out an egg visible at its tail. While the seeds of all metals lie hidden within this egg, through exaltation <note>an alchemical process of raising a substance to a higher state</note> they end in the seven spheres of the Planets. Exerting its power into the Orbs of the metallic planets, it animates and actuates them with heat, so that from there Horus—that is, the Sun and Moon—may emerge through the dissolution of the Elements and the separation of pure things from the impure. For once this is performed, individual things will coalesce with one another through a certain natural and sympathetic love, and this is the completion of the entire work.*

See, Reader, the various things we produce concerning this hierogram in the *Coptic Prodromus* <note>A "forerunner" or introductory treatise on the Coptic language and Egyptian antiquities</note> on page 263.

But since all these things are more obscure than can be perceived by Beginners—inasmuch as they are reserved for those exercised in the art by long labor—it seemed fit in this place, for the sake of <term>philochymia</term> <note>Greek: "love of chemistry/alchemy"</note>, to explain them a little more diffusely, to unroll the hidden secrets into the light, and to show the mode of operating according to the hieroglyphic ideas prescribed in the preceding pages; so that if anyone should please to make the trial, he may have the key by which he can do so.

<margin>The Hermetic character is the key of the Chemical art.</margin>
The entire Hermetic character, composed from all the Figures of the worldly bodies, shows first that a certain power lies hidden, existing in all things, which provides life and nourishment to them; yet it is so concealed that no one, except by the greatest labor, can arrive at a genuine knowledge of it. For it lies hidden in the innermost recesses of natural things, enveloped in the darkness of the central abyss; if anyone knows the unfolding of this, he shall know that the storehouse of all nature is open to him. And he [the author] intended this power to be Mercurial, signified by that manifold character teeming with a progeny of lines; in which there is no distinction of worldly things, but they lie hidden compressed into one, as if in a certain chaos. Yet if you dissolve this, and skillfully distribute it into its members, immediately the orbits of the Planets—not only of the upper World, but also of the lower—will lie open, the elementa-

> <note>Original Arabic text provided in the manuscript</note>

<margin>The opinion of Hermes concerning the essence existing in every thing.</margin>
> *Hermes says that in every thing there exists a living, perpetual, primordial essence, and it is found in every thing and in every house; blessed is he to whom it happens to understand its secret and to handle it properly. He said, moreover, that the secret of this thing is "water," and this water receives its nourishment from men. Marcunes <note>Likely a corruption of Mary the Prophetess or another early alchemical authority</note> also says: all things in the world are sold for more than said water; yet it is with everyone, and everyone needs it; it is with him, nor does it desert him, nor does its spirit depart. Ibn Umayl <note>A famous 10th-century Arab alchemist</note> says, speaking of the said water, that this water is found in every place, in plains, valleys, and mountains; it is found with the rich and the poor, with the strong and the weak. And this is the parable by which all the Wise Men regard their Stone; and it is the water and the moist spirit, and Hermes marked it with the most hidden signs.*

## CHAPTER V.
### How those things which are contained theoretically <note>original: Θεωρικῶς (theorikōs)</note> in the Hermetic character can and ought to be reduced to practice.

<margin>The Hermetic character teaches the practice of Alchemy.</margin>
The Hermetic character beautifully denotes the affinity, property, and nature of the other metals in relation to gold and silver—what must be added to or taken away from each so that it may transform into the Sun <note>Gold</note> or the Moon <note>Silver</note>. This is sketched out by a certain secret likeness to the celestial economy regarding position, place, and nature; from the knowledge of these things, one is led onto the right path—

# CLASS X. HIEROGLYPHIC ALCHEMY. 407 CHAPTER V.

...you are led to the exaltation of individual metals into Sun <note>Gold</note> and Moon <note>Silver</note>, as we shall now reveal.

<image-desc>On the left side of the page is a geometrical construction consisting of two large overlapping circles with vertical and horizontal axes. <margin>The exaltation of the Sun and Moon in the houses of Mars and Venus.</margin>
It must be noted that without the spirits and souls of Mars <note>Iron</note> and Venus <note>Copper</note>, neither the Sun nor the Moon can be exalted. This is indicated by a certain wonderful analogy in the Hermetic character; for Astrology teaches that these two planets, the Sun and Moon, first acquire their exaltations and dignities when they are positioned in the dwellings of Mars and Venus—that is, in Aries and Taurus. Hermes expressed this beautifully through his character <note>symbol</note>, in which you expressly see that the characters of ♂ and ♀ borrow their form from the character of the Sun, just as Saturn ♄ and Jupiter ♃ take theirs from the characters of the Moon, as was demonstrated above. By this it is aptly indicated that just as Mars and Venus are of the nature of the Sun, so Saturn and Jupiter are of the nature of the Moon; and therefore, just as the latter are sympathetic and of the same kind as the Moon, so the former are joined to the Sun by a certain wonderful reason and the hidden laws of friendship. Hence the character of Mars ♂ denotes the Sun by its circle, but by its two semicircles it denotes the character of the horns of Aries ♈—that is, the exaltation of the Sun in Aries, or the dwelling of Mars. That Venus is exalted in Taurus—that is, in her own dwelling—the character ♀ demonstrates well enough; for in this, if you remove the cross, the character ♉ <note>Taurus</note> remains. By this exaltation, Hermes wished to indicate nothing other than that the Sun and Moon in this terrestrial region or globe receive their exaltations and dignities from the terrestrial planets ♂ and ♀, under the guidance of celestial Astrology.

<margin>The common system of the seven planets teaches Alchemy.</margin>
For according to the common system of the Egyptians, Saturn occupies the first place, Jupiter the second, Mars the third, the Sun the fourth, Venus the fifth, Mercury the sixth, and the Moon the seventh. If the planets are now placed in this order, it will certainly be evident from the very arrangement that Mars and Venus participate most closely in the nature of gold, and Saturn and Jupiter in the nature of silver. If Saturn and the Moon, Jupiter and Mercury, and Mars and Venus are joined, then it will always be clear that two share one nature and property, and receive their highest virtue from gold, standing in the middle as the King and center of all. The consensus of the better Chemists agrees with these points, asserting that the Mercury and <term>Sulphur of the Philosophers</term> <note>The active and passive principles of the Great Work, not common chemicals</note>, which feed the gold, provide blood, and urge it on, must be taken and prepared from the <term>tincture</term> <note>The transformative essence or "dye" of a metal</note> of Mars and Venus;

<margin>The tincture of gold</margin>
since the tincture of gold is found to be more abundant in nothing than in Mars and Venus, as if in a male and female. For Venus, through her celestial sulphur, is clothed in celestial splendor; and indeed the tincture which Venus attains is found to be the same in Mars, and even more effective, more excellent, and greater; for Mars is the male, and Venus the female. <margin>A Chemical Secret from Haled.</margin>

> *Here I shall open a secret to you: namely, that gold, copper, and iron contain within themselves one sulfur, one tincture, and one dyeing matter, which matter is a spirit, a vapor, and a smoke—of which we spoke above—which is penetrative of all bodies. If, therefore, you take that and treat it by the spirit which is found in the salt of Mars <note>iron</note>, and mix with that spirit Mercury according to our weight—having first properly purged it of dross and freed and dissolved it from all violent corrosion—know then that you possess a medicine to which nothing in the world can be compared. If indeed it be fermented with the Sun <note>gold</note>, then the entrance will lie open to accomplishing the transmutation of all metals.*

<margin>The weight, fixation, and gradation of the terrestrial Moon are supplied by the remaining planets.</margin>
<image-desc>Alchemical symbol of a circle with a cross mounted on top (The symbol for Antimony or the Earth).</image-desc>
It is also a marvel that since three things are lacking in the terrestrial Moon <note>silver</note>—namely weight, fixation, and gradation—the remaining planets have wished to compensate for those three things in actual practice. Thus, the first defect is weight, and this indeed Saturn <note>lead</note> can restore to it, being closest to the Sun in weight, and called by the Chemists "the leprous Sun." The second defect is fixation; for the Moon, on account of the Mercurial moisture still residing in it and its sulfurous blackness, is not yet cooked out of its impure darkness; hence Mars <note>iron</note>, being closest to the Sun in heat, easily digests the said moisture of the Moon by his fervor, so that it may be exalted to a nobler grade of nature. The third defect is gradation <note>the intensity of color/purity</note>, which Venus, the perpetual companion of the Sun and closest to the Moon in color, easily restores. All of which the more secret Philosophers hinted at not incongruously when they said:

> *Dissolve Venus, congeal her when dissolved, and cast her when congealed upon molten Moon, and she shall be exalted into the color and honor of the truest and brightest Sun.*

<margin>A Chemical Axiom and its interpretation.</margin>
Which indeed, according to the interpretation of our character <note>symbol</note>, is to be understood thus: Venus is the exaltation of the Moon to the degree of the Sun; therefore calcine Venus, let her overflow, sublime her, dissolve her, and join the solution to the dissolved Moon; congeal this, and you shall have the exaltation of the Sun. Its tincture and weight are ascribed to Mars (for they are easily transmuted into one another), who, if he is transmuted into Saturn, is called the "Saturn of the Philosophers," for under these two a perfect fixation lies hidden and enclosed. For if you dry out the phlegmatic constitution of the Moon through the hot blood of Venus, and correct her blackness through the salt of Mars, then the spirit of Mars, the constancy of the Moon, and the beauty of Venus will harmonize perfectly in mixture and concord.

<margin>The Hermetic Character teaches how the three defects of the terrestrial Moon are to be supplied.</margin>
But what proportion these three bodies have, and what portion of mixing they require, is evident from the characterization of Hermes. For since the Moon is subject to three defects, one must first consider the qualities and nature, and which of those defects is the greatest, and what is appropriate first—that is, digestion—and what is last—that is, tincture; and then by how much Saturn exceeds these in weight; furthermore, the astronomical position and proximity to the Sun must be observed, as we taught above. If you now have a mind to transmute the Moon into the Sun, it is neces—

# CLASS X. HIEROGLYPHIC ALCHEMY 409 CHAPTER V.

<margin>The practice of the Egyptians in Chemical matters.</margin>
It is necessary that the most subtle tinting spirits be extracted from *Mars* <note>iron</note> and *Venus* <note>copper</note> and fermented with gold; and if *Luna* <note>silver</note> is to become *Sol* <note>gold</note>, those two Planets, *Mercurius* <note>quicksilver</note> and *Venus*, which stand between *Sol* and *Luna*, must first be separated. Then the blackness departs with *Venus*, and the evaporating humidity with *Mercurius*. For this, salts, strong waters <note>acids</note>, and vegetable matter are required; for through these, bodies are purified and take on a spiritual substance. Do you see, therefore, how many secrets *Hermes* <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note> has hidden under this hieroglyphic character? But so that we may come closer to the truth of these sayings, let us subjoin the practice used by the Egyptians as related by the Arabs.

<margin>The Hermetic Character teaches the dissolution of metallic matter into its elements.</margin>
It must be known, therefore, that the key to the whole art consists in the dissolution of metallic matter into its Elements through fire and putrefaction; for a body that has not been putrefied produces no form. However, once putrefied by the service of fire, it is then resolved by distillation. Thus, the seven *metallic Planets* must first be resolved into four distinct natures: that is, into *calx* <note>powdered oxide or ash</note>, into *salt*, into *water*, and into *oil*, which is the *Mercury of the Philosophers*, the end of the entire operation. All of these are aptly shown in our Hermetic character by the *Cross*, in which the lowest line beautifully represents the earthly metallic substance or calx; the side lines represent the salt and water; and finally, the upper line represents the fiery substance or oil, which must be drawn out from the presupposed matter. Know, therefore, that the said seven metallic bodies shown in the Hermetic diagram can first be reduced to calx, then from calx becomes salt, after salt comes water, and from water finally the *Philosophical Mercury*; this is the soul of any resolved metal, having the power to transmute things similar to itself into the best state.

<margin>Calcination is the beginning of the Chemical work.</margin>
The beginning of the work, therefore, is the *calcination of metals* <note>heating to high temperatures to create an ash</note>, so that from the preparation of the *calx*, *salt* may then be extracted, which the Arabs call *bitter salt* or *vinegar*. Nothing else is to be attended to in the work except the extraction of *salts*; for these *salts* contain within themselves the transforming soul of the metals, by which all metals, through the sole operation of nature, are transmuted into nobler and nobler metals. For it has a penetrating power on account of its supreme subtlety and sharpness. It must be known, however, that *Sol* and *Luna* alone have the virtue and power of fixing the salts of the other imperfect metals—especially those which produce a calx similar to the calx of *Sol*, that is, *citrine* <note>yellow-orange</note>; but the salts of those which produce a *white* calx are similar to the calx of *Luna*, as will be said in what follows.

<margin>The Hermetic Character teaches which things are in sympathy with the Sun and Moon.</margin>
<margin>The calcination of the individual metallic planets.</margin>
Which of the imperfect metals are in sympathy with *Sol* and which with *Luna*, the Hermetic Character beautifully shows, as we taught above. For those [sympathetic to the Sun] are ♄ *Saturn* or lead, ♀ *Venus* or copper, and ♂ *Mars* or iron. But those sympathetic to *Luna* are ♃ *Jupiter* or tin, and ☿ *Mercury*. For just as the former Planets produce a citrine calx, so these produce a white calx; each of which, being led into salt, then water, and finally into oil, acquires the power of transmuting into *Luna*. With these things forewarned, nothing remains except that we also show in a few words the calcination of the individual metallic Planets, which we have gathered from the works of Hermes as reported in Arabic by *Haled* <note>likely referring to Khalid ibn Yazid, an early Umayyad prince associated with alchemy</note>. Nor should anyone think that I place faith in them, since—

# CHAPTER V. THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM OF THE EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS.

I have not learned these things by practical experiment, but as befits an "Oedipus" <note>Kircher refers to himself as Oedipus, the solver of riddles, implying he is interpreting these mysteries intellectually rather than as a practicing chemist.</note>, I have wished only to set them forth—as I do all other matters of this sort—by abstracting them from all questions of truth or falsehood.

<margin>The Calcination of the Sun (Gold).</margin>
First, let the Sun <note>Gold</note> be beaten into thin plates and cleansed of all filth; then, by the aid of Antimony, let it be calcined in a reverberatory furnace <note>A furnace that reflects heat onto the material</note> in an open vessel for six continuous days. Once reduced to a lime <note>A powder or oxide</note>, it shall be washed with rain water (or even better, with May-dew) and distilled; the more often this is done, the better. Mix this with the lime, place it in a glass vessel, and cook it over hot ashes for the space of one natural day, until the lime has imbibed and consumed all the water. Then, place this lime back into the reverberatory furnace and calcine it again for one natural day, repeating the washing just as before. Repeat this operation ten or twelve times until it reaches its perfection; the sign of which will be a most pure lime, entirely golden, clear, and shining; whence it is called the *Cerusse of the Sun*.

<margin>The Calcination of Venus (Copper).</margin>
The second Planet sympathetic to the Sun is Venus ♀, namely copper. It is calcined in a reverberatory furnace or a glass-making furnace for ten days, which the symbol <term>⊛</term> <note>original: "⊛ circulo annexa"</note>—a circle attached to a cross, the symbol of the denarius—clearly shows. One must proceed as above, re-calcining it until it has acquired a red tincture like that of blood; it is then called the *Cerusse of Venus*.

<margin>The Calcination of Mars (Iron).</margin>
The third Planet sympathetic to the Sun is ♂ Mars, that is, iron. You shall calcine and re-calcine this for ten days in the said furnace, and wash it as many times,

<margin>The Calcination of Saturn (Lead).</margin>
until the lime has obtained a very red tincture. The fourth Planet sympathetic to the Sun is ♄ Saturn <note>Lead</note>, which you shall transform into its cerusse in exactly the same manner as described above.

<margin>The Calcination of the Moon (Silver) and the other planets.</margin>
The Moon <note>Silver</note> and the other planets sympathetic to her are calcined thus: The Moon must be placed in a closed vessel for a period of ten days, proceeding with the washing as was said above regarding the calcination of the Sun. You will then have a most clear and shining *Cerusse of the Moon*, leaning somewhat toward blue. In calcining ♃ Jupiter <note>Tin</note>, which is sympathetic to the Moon, proceed with equal steps in all things, and you will have the *Cerusse of Jupiter*. However, the calcination of ☿ Mercury, which is sympathetic to the Moon, is handled a little differently since it is of a fleeting nature. You shall proceed as follows: First, Mercury shall be dissolved in *aqua fortis* <note>Nitric acid</note> with two parts alum and one part saltpeter. Once dissolved, pour over it a little lukewarm spring water in which you have sprinkled a little common salt; immediately the Mercury will seek the bottom in the form of a white lime. When this is done, remove the water from the vessel and wash the lime as above, and you will have your goal.

<margin>How the Salt is extracted from the lime of each metallic planet.</margin>
Having obtained the lime of the seven metals, you shall extract the salt from the lime of each by this industry: Take the lime of whichever Planet you wish, place it in a vessel, and pour over it the best vinegar, distilled three or four times. Place this over hot ashes; and when the vinegar has warmed slightly with the lime, set the vessel down and allow the mixture to cool until a fine sediment forms. Then, with the greatest care so that it does not mix with the lime, draw off the water. Place it in an alembic <note>A distilling apparatus</note> and distill it over hot ashes with a slow fire, and you will have the vinegar. When you see the first signs of beginning congealment, remove the alembic and let it cool; it will be bound together into a most beautiful and shining salt.

The purpose of this salt is to transmute the combustible and defective natures of imperfect metals into perfect ones, such as Gold and Silver <note>original: "Sol & Luna"</note>, according to the sympathy which each has for either the Sun or the Moon. <margin>The salt of individual metals.</margin> The Salt of Saturn <note>Lead</note> is called Saltpeter, of a most shining color. <margin>Haled the Arab <note>Referring to Khalid ibn Yazid, an early Umayyad prince and alchemist.</note></margin>
> Hermes said: Take the sulfur, the smoke, the vapor, and the quicksilver—which is the Bitter Salt—take it and distill it with a fire-tool, using the heat of charcoal. Return its water as before and distill it; there will distill for you a vinegar, leaving no dross or impurity behind. This is the Vinegar of Hermes and the vinegar of all the Sages. In this saying is an indication of the four elements contained within the Bitter Salt, and its state through the aforementioned preparation as a distilled vinegar. It is the Permissible Water called the Water of Life. Indeed, this water burns bodies like fire and preserves them from burning like water; it washes them like soap from filth, calcines them like sulfur, and dissolves them like quicksilver. This water is a frozen fire, a cold snow, a dissolved sulfur, and a fixed quicksilver like a white pearl. This is the secret of the hidden life in all things; therefore, it revives the earth after its death and is called the Water of Life. ۞

<margin>The opinion of Hermes regarding the water of life.</margin>
Hermes said: take sulfur, and smoke, and vapor, and quicksilver, namely that which is called Bitter Salt, and it is the Mercury of the Philosophers; they take this and distill it over a slow fire, strengthening it gradually with the fire of coals, and they distill according to the art bit by bit, directing it until, the water being consumed, nothing else flows; then you shall allow the whole to cool in its place, and let the water be poured on a second time, and you shall distill it, and there will be distilled for you a most purified vinegar, and this is the Hermetic vinegar, and the vinegar of all the Philosophers, and in this you have everything that is in the bitter salt from the four elements, and upon its essence in the mentioned mastery of distilled vinegar; and it is a praiseworthy water, and is called the water of life; since this water burns all things like fire, and preserves them from combustion like water, and washes them like soap from impurity, and calcines <term>calcination: reducing a metal to powder by heat</term> them like sulfur, and dissolves them like Mercury, and this water is a congealed fire, cold snow, and dissolved sulfur, and fixed quicksilver like a white Pearl <note>original: "Unionis candidi"</note>, and this is the secret of life, and it is found in all things; by this the earth lives after its death, and it is called the water of life. <margin>The hieroglyphic of the Beetle teaches the secret of the water of life.</margin> These things are indeed aptly explained by the previous Beetle-shaped <note>Scarab-shaped</note> hieroglyphic; in which the Beetle signifies the primary matter of the seven metals agitated by the Mundane Spirit, having an appetite for all forms; in it is a diversity of colors, that is, golden, green, red, white, black, sky-blue, bright white (for the Sun-Beetle <note>Heliocantharus</note> exhibits all these colors in its body), representing the various colors which we behold in the process of the Chemical work,

It renders the body volatile; that is, when the body has been dissolved in this vinegar, it ascends to the surface of the water. <margin>The Elixir of the Philosophers according to Khalid and Artephius.</margin> Thus, however, the work proceeds by the instruction of Mercury, Khalid <note>original: "Haled," referring to Khalid ibn Yazid, an early Umayyad prince associated with alchemy.</note>, and Artephius—whoever that man of a thousand years <term>long-lived <note>original Greek: μακρόβιος (makrobios)</note></term> might have been, who is ignorantly imagined in this place to have prolonged his life solely by the use of his elixir. Thus the perfect body of the Sun <note>Gold</note> receives life in such water; it is quickened, inspired, grows, and multiplies in its own species, just like all other things. For this vinegar, when mixed with the Sun and Moon <note>Gold and Silver</note>, adheres to them, and the bodies receive from it a tincture of shining whiteness. Therefore, he who knows how to convert the body into white medicinal silver will thereafter, with no trouble, convert all imperfect metals into the best silver by increasing in it its native heat, weight, substance, and tincture. For as soon as it feels the heat enclosed within itself, if the perfect body of the Sun and Moon be in it, it will split it and liquefy it into a white substance similar to itself in silver color, weight, and tincture. # CHAPTER V. 414 EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

<margin>As soon as the living water is dissolved, let it be congealed.</margin>
<margin>The effect of living water.</margin>
...natural, by which the perfect bodies of the Sun and Moon <note>Gold and Silver</note> are resolved through a certain wondrous metamorphosis, while preserving their species and without any destruction, except toward a new, nobler, and better form; so that, once the resolution is made, it may finally be congealed with them, fixed, and constrained into a "white earth." It is also marvelous that as soon as this water is dissolved, it is congealed at the very same time; for one is not dissolved without the other being congealed. Therefore, when you see the water congealing itself with the bodies dissolved in it, know that you are proceeding on the right path to the completion of the work. And since it is impossible for hard and dry bodies to be intimately penetrated and dyed without dissolution, our water has obtained this gift from nature: to destroy, change, and convert bodies and metallic forms into a moist, soft, and fluid substance, so that it can be imbued intimately and to the marrow with a perfect tincture. Hence gold is not dyed unless its spirit is extracted from its center by this water of ours and reduced into a quasi-spiritual substance, which the Sages call "white smoke," "spirit," and "soul." All these things, signified through the anatomy of the Scarab-shaped hieroglyphic mentioned above, are beautifully demonstrated. For it is impossible for that which is intended to be born from the Spirit of the World, unless Horus and Isis—that is, the Sun and Moon—are separated from the earthly body and its various subject imperfections through the separation of the Elements, and hidden within an egg, and thus finally, actuated by a friendly attraction, condensed into a yolk and albumen, which is the final completion of the work.

<margin>Living water makes an incombustible oil from dissolved gold and silver.</margin>
Furthermore, as soon as the water has dissolved the gold and silver, it makes an **incombustible oil**, which, when mixed with other imperfect metals, elevates them and leads them back to that from which they were drawn; for it converts them into the nature of a fusible salt, which the Arabs call <term>Sal Albroth</term> <note>original Arabic: *al-milh al-barun*; likely referring to a purified or "white" salt used in the Great Work</note>; and it is a most noble salt, fixed, subtle, penetrating, permeating all the inner marrow of bodies, the <term>Complete Elixir</term>, the <term>Secret of Secrets</term> ✢ <note>original Arabic: *Sirr al-Asrar*</note>, that is, the *greatest secret of secrets*. Hence it is said by Haled <note>Khalid ibn Yazid, a famous early Umayyad prince and alchemist</note>:

> <term>Whoever knows the salt of the Sun and Moon and its generation, and knows how to mix it with the aforementioned bodies</term>
> <term>and knows the Secret of Secrets ✢</term>

And this is that *Mercury of the Philosophers*, of which we spoke above—not at all, as the common people think, that ordinary quicksilver—yet it is hidden in the innermost retreat of it, as it is in the other metals of the Sun and Moon. From these three, and no others—Mercury, Moon, and Sun—as if from a certain mystical triad, the *so-called Philosopher's Stone* is composed. Its body is the fixed, most subtle Solar earth, raised up by the power of our water; its soul is the tincture <note>The transformative essence or color</note> of the Sun and Moon; its spirit, however, is the mineral power of both and of the water, which carries the tincture or soul above the bodies and out of the bodies. Therefore, just as the penetrating spirit fixes the body, so the soul joins, colors, and whitens; and without these three, all labor in the Chemical business is in vain. Therefore, dissolve the bodies in our aforementioned water, and digest them with a tempered heat, until the entire tincture goes forth through the water into a white color or a white oil. Place these same bodies together with our water in a Hermetic vessel <note>A glass flask sealed with heat</note> hermetically sealed, over a slow fire, and digest them until they are resolved into oil; which, by a very slow distillation over a long time, finally provides what you seek. Let there be, however, as I said, a gentle and continuous fire, until they are dissolved into a viscous water, and the entire tincture goes forth, first in the color of blackness, which is the sign of true dissolution. Finally, continue the decoction until it becomes a permanent white water; for in its own bath it will acquire a luster and clarity similar to common Mercury, being exalted above the surface of the first water. Thus, when you see the bodies dissolved into a viscous water, let that be a sign to you that the bodies are now converted into vapor, and that you possess the souls separated from the dead bodies and carried up in the Sublimation of the Choir of Spirits. There, the body composed of male and female—that is, of Sun and Moon—receives from that most subtle nature, purified by sublimation, a life that is vegetative and capable of multiplying itself. And from this it is clear why our Hermetic hieroglyphic character <note>The symbol of Mercury/Hermes</note> explained above expresses this Solar-Lunar-Mercurial tri-unity above all; while the other planets are established under them only by happenstance.

<margin>What the elemental fire ought to be like in chemistry <note>original: "chimia"</note>.</margin>
Fittingly, therefore, they expressed a twofold fire through the horns: one physical, the other virtual. The first is Elemental, but with a certain proportion of intensity, such as that of a lamp constructed for this purpose with singular industry and ingenuity; nor does any greater difficulty present itself in the entire ministry of the Great Art than in properly proportioning this fire, and tempering it with a most precise proportion, so that it may finally achieve the hoped-for effect.

<margin>The tempering of heat is most necessary and most difficult in the Chemical art.</margin>
Consequently, I certainly believe that this business meets with such unhappy outcomes, even among philosophers of the highest reputation, for no other reason than that they do not know the temperament of heat necessary to complete the operation of nature. But since we have reserved this material for the third book of *The Subterranean World* <note>Kircher's famous work *Mundus Subterraneus*</note>, which we call Metallic Geography—where we shall professedly describe the lamp or Hermetic furnace according to the mind of the Arabs—we do not wish to be more lengthy here. Therefore, at the beginning of our second operation, the fire must be continuous, moist, vaporous, airy, and prepared with artificial industry and no less judgment; for if the lamp or furnace lacks its due Geometric proportion, certainly through a defect of heat the signs will not appear at the designated time, or through an excess of heat the flowers of gold will be burned, with the effort of the entire business becoming utterly void and vanished. Therefore, either the lamp, or the furnace, or the ashes, or the dung containing the proportioned heat, must be so prepared that, once the Hermetically sealed vessel is placed upon it, you may obtain the desired effect through circulation.

<margin>Mineral fire in the Chemical art.</margin>
The second fire is in our natural Philosophical water, which is also called the fire against nature, as we have shown above from *Haled* <note>Referring to Khalid ibn Yazid, an early Umayyad prince associated with alchemy</note>; because it is water, and it makes a spirit out of gold, which Elemental fire cannot provide. For it is mineral, and implanted in metals from the beginning; it also participates in sulfur, destroys all things, congeals, dissolves, calcines, penetrates any innermost marrow, is incombustible, and is the source of living water—necessary to the craftsman in the beginning, middle, and end—the architect of nature, which works only the temperament of artificial fire. But let these things suffice concerning fire. Let us now proceed to explain the conditions of the colors occurring in the Hermetic work.

<margin>The four colors in the Hermetic work.</margin>
Know, therefore, that four principal kinds of colors present themselves, which are aptly expressed by the four-part Cross of our Hermetic character: black, white, red, and yellow <note>original: "citrinus"</note>, from which all other species of colors are born. The color which is not black cannot whiten; for blackness is the beginning of whiteness, and a sign of putrefaction and alteration, and it provides a sign that the body has now been penetrated and multiplied. Therefore, in the work, blackness first appears like a pepper broth; then, by the continuation of the cooking <note>term: "coction" (the process of heating or "ripening" the alchemical matter)</note>, it degenerates into whiteness and floats on top like white cream. This is a sign of the union of the spirits gathered in that indissoluble bond: for when the whiteness appears, the dark dominion of the moist nature soon perishes, and a white smoke penetrates into the new body—resuscitated, clear, white, and immortal—and triumphs by carrying away the victory from all injuries. It is therefore the completion of the entire work or of the Philosopher's Stone (which should be well noted), so that a perfect body may be formed,

It should be kept in a digestion of gentle heat—such as a water bath or very tempered manure—and the urgency of the work must be continued through the fire of perfect decoction <note>The process of heating a substance in liquid to extract its essence</note> until it putrefies and is resolved into black, and then elevated into white. For just as heat acting upon moisture generates blackness as the first color, so continued heat upon dryness generates whiteness as the second color, and thereafter yellowness and redness by acting upon pure dryness. Therefore, whiten the black and redden the white so that you may complete the work. When you see the true whiteness appear, striking the sharp gaze of the eyes with its brilliance, know that the redness is hidden within the whiteness. Then the decoction must only be continued so that, with dryness and heat, there supervenes yellowness and a most shining redness. When you see this, praise God, because you have finally found what the world so greatly desires, so studiously seeks, and considers worth acquiring through so many cares and labors.

# CHAPTER VI.

## Explanations of several hieroglyphics concerning the practice of the Hermetic art.

<margin>The ignorance of some pseudo-alchemists.</margin>
I would be excessive if I were to bring forward here the enigmas, riddles, parables, and secret pronouncements with which most pseudo-alchemists <note>original: "Chimiastri"; a derogatory term for those practicing "puffery" or false chemistry</note> of this time have veiled their sacraments—or more truly, their trifles and delusions. Of these, nothing more foolish or more impertinent to the matter can be said; so much so, that it appears at first glance to be entirely vain and fabricated, being blurted out so awkwardly, so disconnectedly, and with such a rough confusion full of contradictions. Added to this is the extreme corruption of the authors they cite, or the tradition of when each lived, which is utterly inconsistent. For first, they make Hermes Trismegistus a King of Constantinople—the ruler, forsooth, of a city not yet existing in the nature of things! <note>Constantinople was founded in the 4th century AD, long after the legendary Hermes Trismegistus was said to have lived.</note>
<margin>The lies of the pseudo-alchemists.</margin>
Next, they cite several Arabian Kings as alchemists, invented at their own whim to win some authority for their imposture, even though no mention of them is made in all of Arabian history or the chemical manuscripts in my possession. They say, moreover, that Artephius <note>A famous medieval alchemical author</note> lived for a thousand years by the use of the universal medicine.
<margin>The fabulous longevity of Artephius.</margin>
But as to what time or century he lived in, there is deep silence from everyone. For if he lived for a thousand years, and after Christ (as his book indicates), I ask: under which Pope or Emperor did this new Methuselah live for so many years with an age unheard of by the world—an age much more advanced than the first Methuselah before the flood? For such a notable miracle would have rightly occupied the pens of all writers, and would have undoubtedly drawn Kings and Princes with the greediest curiosity to consult such an oracle about the events of past times. You see, therefore, how these chemists, to win some esteem for their art, feign anything with the audacity of a hardened brow; how without judgment they everywhere devise things which...

# CHAPTER VI. 418 EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

<margin>The books called the *Assembly of the Philosophers* are barbarous.</margin>
Just as these works cannot be supported by any reason, so it cannot be said how much contempt they bring upon their art, and how much damage they do to its reputation. Such are the things thrust upon us by the work entitled *The Assembly of the Philosophers* <note>original: *Turba Philosophorum*, a famous early Latin alchemical text</note>, which is full of horrendous barbarism, stuffed with fictional authors and ridiculous old wives' tales. There is hardly a page where the same "reheated cabbage" <note>A Latin idiom for a boring, repeated story</note> is not served up again. Everything in it that is excellent or rare could easily be contained within the space of a single leaf. I advise all who wish to philosophize soundly to beware of them.

<margin>The wisdom of the Egyptians in delivering Chemistry through hieroglyphs.</margin>
The Egyptians surely delivered their knowledge to posterity more wisely. As seen above, they used a single hieroglyph to encompass a doctrine of metallic succession—something others cannot achieve even with vast books. However, they wrapped this doctrine in symbols so that the key to the secrets was handed to no one except those whose office required it. I do not deny that the universal doctrine of the "Divine" <note>original: *τῆς θείας* (tēs theias)</note> Hermetic art truly exists, confirmed by the testimony of so many noble authors from the beginning. But I say it is so hidden that access to such inexhaustible riches is prepared only for a few Philosophers, and those who have been practiced for a long time in judgment and every kind of natural science. I would also call him blessed who, through a "blessed error," eventually comes to the knowledge of the art. But we have dealt with these matters more fully in the first chapter; therefore, let us pursue the material proposed to us. First, as befits an "Oedipus" <note>The author refers to himself as Oedipus, the solver of riddles</note>, I will interpret some modern enigmas, having been urged to do so by the insistence of many; then I will set down some Egyptian hieroglyphic inscriptions alluding to this, so that I may fulfill my promises.

### The First Chemical Enigma, and its explanation.

<margin>The first Chemical Enigma.</margin>
The following Enigma contains two parts: in the first part, the thing to be solved is described; in the second, the Sphinx itself. The wits of many have sweated over the unraveling of this. For some have attempted to twist it toward a moral sense; others toward an allegorical one. <margin>William Baroldon.</margin> William Baroldon, an Englishman, explains it in a Cabalistic sense in his book on the true and genuine interpretation of Holy Scripture through the Cabalistic art. The author of *The Delights of the World* attempts to investigate it through a metathetic combination of letters <note>Rearranging letters, like an anagram</note>. Others want the Enigma to be composed of "equal numerical value" <note>original: *τὴν ἰσοψηφίαν* (tēn isopshēphian)</note>, from the class of riddles <margin>Grunderus.</margin> which the Greeks call "equal pebbles" <note>original: *τὰ ἰσόψηφα* (ta isopshēpha) - Gematria, where words have equal numerical sums</note>. So says Grunderus. We shall briefly set forth what we think, what the matter is, and how it is to be solved by a physical method.

<margin>Explanation of the first Enigma.</margin>
> *Aelia Laelia Crispis, neither man, nor woman, nor Androgynous, nor girl, nor old woman, nor chaste, nor a whore, nor modest, but all of these. Taken away neither by hunger, nor by sword, nor by poison, but by all of them. She lies neither in heaven, nor in the waters, nor in the earth, but everywhere. Lucius Agatho Priscius, neither husband, nor lover, nor kinsman, neither mourning, nor rejoicing, nor weeping, knows and knows not for whom he has placed this, which is neither a mound, nor a pyramid, nor a tomb, but all of them.*

# CLASS 10. HIEROGLYPHIC ALCHEMY. 419 CHAPTER 6.

the Chemical art. It is called *Aelia Laelia* because it was always held in great value by the Roman Emperors of the *Aelian* name, and by the *Laelii*, men of ancient nobility among the Romans; and it was cultivated at all times with a great expenditure of wealth, as can be seen in the writings of Eutropius on the Roman Emperors, Suetonius, Lampridius, Rhodiginus, and other writers of Roman history. *Rypsis* <note>original: "Rypsis"</note> is, by way of an anagram or through the transposition of letters, the same as *Pyrsis*, or in Greek *Pyrsis* <note>original: Πύρσις</note>, which properly signifies an empirical refinement, specifically when we refine something by means of fire. Nothing else is suggested here but that Elixir of life, or as they commonly call it, the Philosopher's Stone <term>Lapis philosophicus: the legendary substance capable of turning base metals into gold and granting immortality</term>, transmuted from metals into a certain admirable substance by the various modification and tempering of fire.

**Neither man, nor woman.** Among all Alchemists, two principles, as it were, are required to produce the Philosopher's Stone which converts all things into gold: namely, sulfur and mercury <note>original: "hydrargyron seu argentum vivum"</note>; the former is like the active principle, the latter like the passive. <margin>Geber. Trismegistus.</margin> And therefore, by Geber <note>An 8th-century Arab alchemist, often cited as the father of chemistry</note> and Trismegistus <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical author of the Hermetic Corpus</note> in the *Emerald Tablet* <note>A foundational text of alchemy</note>, they are frequently called "man" and "woman" under an obscure veil of words. These things being established, we explain this paragraph thus: *The Philosopher's Stone is neither man nor woman*, that is, it is neither sulfur nor mercury, because it has already been transmuted into another substance, with the substance or essence of neither of the aforementioned remaining, as is the common opinion of Chemists. It is, however, man and woman, because it consists of them as its material principles.

Furthermore, it is said, **Nor Androgynous.** By "Androgynous" is understood an animal endowed with both sexes. The Philosopher's Stone, by way of similarity, is said to be both not Androgynous and Androgynous; Androgynous because it consists of both as its principles, namely sulfur and mercury; not Androgynous because nothing of the aforementioned remained in the refinement made of this stone.

**Neither girl, nor old woman.** By these words it is signified that this stone (or as others call it, the *vegetable egg*) is present in things from the beginning of the world as something vile and despised, which is signified by "old woman"; however, insofar as it is rescued from earthly dross by the industry of the Chemical art, it is called a "girl," as if established in her youthful beauty. It is called "neither girl nor old woman" because human industry could not refine it so much that something of its ancient and earthly concretion did not remain.

**Neither chaste, nor a prostitute, nor modest, but all things.** It is called first chaste and not chaste, modest and not modest, a prostitute and not a prostitute; <margin>Geber. Raymond Lull.</margin> for as Geber rightly feels, and with him Raymond Lull <note>A 13th-century philosopher and alchemist</note> in his book *On the Fifth Essence*, no thing can be so refined by human industry that something of the earth does not remain. Since, therefore, the stone is not an Element, nor a simple body, but composed of the four Elements, it is clear why it is called chaste and not chaste, which is the same as pure and not pure, etc.

**Taken away neither by hunger, nor by the sword, nor by poison, but by all.** This means that just as a single grain can never sprout or even grow unless it first dies after being cast into the earth; so also the Philosopher's Stone can never reach that transformative growth <note>original: "vegetationem conversivam"</note> unless it is first mortified by certain specific means; namely by "hunger," that is, by calcination, fixation, and coagula-

# CHAPTER VI. 420 EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

<note>The title refers to Athanasius Kircher's massive work "Oedipus Aegyptiacus," where he attempts to "solve" the riddles of Egyptian hieroglyphs through an alchemical and mystical lens.</note>

...by purification; by iron, that is, the saffron of Mars <note>original: "croco Martis" — a reddish-brown iron oxide used in alchemy</note>, or the purest flowers of iron; and finally by poison, that is, crude or refined antimony. However, it is not so completely "killed" <note>mortified or transformed</note> by these means that a root of earthly dross does not always remain, as has been said. It lies neither in heaven, nor in earth, nor in the waters, but everywhere. These details again suggest a certain contradiction, which must nevertheless be understood according to different perspectives. It is not in the earth, because it has been separated from all earthly concretion as far as human industry allows; nor in the waters, since it stands far elevated above watery matter as a more subtle substance; nor in the heavens, since it is not a simple body, and yet it is composed of all of them. And it is found in all things: in the earth indeed, insofar as it is the primary matter of this Stone; in the waters, insofar as that earth, when dissolved, turns into a watery substance, or also because <term>psammon</term> <note>original: "ψάμμον" — Greek for sand</note> or golden sand, which is found here and there scattered in rivers, is taken by many as the material for this Stone; and finally, it is in the heavens by its influential power.

### The Second Chemical Enigma, and its Explanation.

<margin>Hamuel Sadid.</margin>
<margin>The second Chemical Enigma.</margin>
This enigma, extracted from the monuments of the Egyptians by the Arab Hamuel Sadid, is as follows. It displays an aged man in a temple, elevated on a throne and surrounded by a crowd of Philosophers; with both hands he displays two tablets resting on his knees. On the first tablet are seen three Moons, two of which are full, with two birds between them; the lower bird is without wings, while the upper one is conspicuous for its spreading wings. The upper bird, standing face-down upon the other, bites its tail, while the lower one bites the tail of the upper. On the second tablet, three Suns are seen, bright with the spreading of rays, the two upper ones being connected to the lower one as if by their rays. From the side, ten eagles are perceived in the act and posture of flying. And this is the Enigma, which I explain all the more gladly for having been extracted from Egyptian monuments, as it has a great affinity to the hieroglyphic symbols to be introduced shortly.

<image-desc>A woodcut illustration depicting an elderly, bearded man (identified in the text as Hermes Trismegistus) seated on a high-backed throne within a temple-like architectural setting. He holds two tablets resting on his knees. The left tablet displays three crescent moons and two birds positioned tail-to-beak; the right tablet shows three radiant suns with connecting rays. He is flanked by a crowd of standing men (philosophers). On the left side of the scene, ten eagles are shown in flight.</image-desc>

<margin>Explanation of the second enigma.</margin>
The temple or house in which the pictures are seen denotes nothing other than the Hermetic or Mineral World, in which all things are hidden, wrapped together as if in a certain chaos. The aged man, full of majesty and residing on the throne, denotes Hermes Trismegistus, the first explorer of the Mineral World and the father of all Philosophers. The crowd of men surrounding the throne on the right and left denotes Philosophers of a twofold condition; those on the right denote those who, being sufficiently instructed in science and the knowledge of things, approach the scrutiny of the Hermetic art...

# CLASS X. HIEROGLYPHIC ALCHEMY. 421 CHAPTER VI.

<margin>What the individual parts of the chemical Enigma denote.</margin>
They indeed enter, but have not yet attained perfection in the same due to the difficulty of the work; nevertheless, driven by curiosity, they demand instruction from Hermes so that they may finally arrive at that which they so greatly desire. Those, however, who stand around on the left denote those Philosophers who, while not equipped with a sufficient supply of knowledge of things, attempt to penetrate the sublime inner sanctuaries of these matters with "unwashed hands," as the saying goes <note>A Latin idiom meaning to approach a sacred or difficult task without proper preparation or reverence</note>; and it is certain that these men will never complete anything in their work. Hermes, therefore, venerable in his majesty, holds a double tablet placed in his lap: through the first, by three Moons and two birds joined into one, the first preparation of the <term>Lunarium</term> <note>The "Lunar" or silver-making work</note> is noted; through the other tablet, by three radiant Suns, two of which are joined by rays into a visible form, the preparation of the <term>Solarium</term> <note>The "Solar" or gold-making work</note> is denoted. Thus, five elements in the first Tablet and just as many in the second, arranged not without ingenuity, occur as the primary things to be considered—five pertaining to the Lunar operation and five to the Solar. Above the throne of Hermes, ten Eagles are seen, conspicuous with their wings spread, each of which is equipped with a bow and arrow. But let us look at the secret, though we have deliberately omitted their figures here.

<margin>The first part of the chemical tablet.</margin>
First, the tablet is divided into two parts, and it signifies two operations in the chemical business, the first of which is occupied with the making of the Moon <note>Silver</note>, and the second with the making of the Sun <note>Gold</note>. Through the upper Lunar figures, of which the first is <term>dichotomos</term> <note>original Greek: διχότομος; meaning cut in half or a half-moon</note> and the second is <term>panselenos</term> <note>original Greek: πανσέληνος; meaning a full moon</note>, a double Moon is indicated. The one which is half-full involves imperfection; the full one denotes that which is capable of increase, until finally it produces that other inferior Moon, by no means common, which the Philosophers call <term>Mercurial water</term>, <term>white silver</term>, <note>original: argentum album</note> <term>white smoke</term>, <term>white earth</term>, and <term>magnetic earth</term>, and by similar names. This is by no means reached except through putrefaction, thinning, and the abstraction of the soul from the body in the spiritual water, which is indicated by two birds. Of these, the lower one without wings indicates the male, and the other with wings, which stands upon the first, indicates the female; they are shown mutually devouring each other's tails. These two birds are two and yet one; for the water made from two vapors, indicated by the <term>uripygia</term> <note>A term referring to the "tail-biting" or Uroboros-like connection of the birds</note>, makes one out of two by congealing and reducing them into one. Moreover, the birds seem to restrain themselves, because that which was first dissolved from two now becomes one when congealed; for the male deprived of wings—that is, the congealed part—retains the flying female—that is, the Mercurial spirit—lest she be able to flee, and forces her to remain with him. Therefore, they are seen bound together and as if compacted into one; this is the true fixation of the full white Moon. And this is confirmed by the saying of Hermes found in Haled <note>Referring to Khalid ibn Yazid, an early Umayyad prince associated with alchemy</note>:

<margin>Haled.</margin>
> *Cast the female upon the male, and the male shall ascend upon the female, and you have what you desire.* <note>original Arabic: ارمي الامره على الدكر ويصعد الدكر على الامراء وتحصل كل ما تريد</note>

For as the Arabs rightly say, their stone is prepared from five things: the male, the female, and a triple quicksilver; which are indeed aptly noted by the triple Moon and the two birds biting each other's tails. <term>Mercurial water</term> is not glued together except with a sulfur similar to itself dwelling in the center of the water, nor is anything else found similar to sulfur except that which is from itself: for, as Hermes witnesses, that which is more closely related fits the thing...

# CHAPTER VI. 422 EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

<margin>Likeness</margin>...from its own nature; for foreign and dissimilar things utterly reject any association. For just as a tree, whose branches, leaves, flowers, and fruits are from it, through it, and for it, is itself the whole, and the whole is from it, nor does any thing ever generate others except from that which is of the same species as itself: so it happens exactly in the <term>Hermetic business</term> <note>The "Hermetic business" refers to the practice of alchemy, named after Hermes Trismegistus.</note>, in which many and diverse things seem to concur, which are nevertheless one thing by their nature, and tend toward one end, as the figure teaches. Take, therefore, the <term>Lunar materials</term> <note>Silver or mercury-based substances in alchemical symbolism.</note> at the beginning of the fresh work; let them be mixed equally and ground, then let them be wedded and crushed one into the other so that a conception may occur; afterward let them be extracted and nourished so that a birth may happen. Truly, this conception and wedding does not occur except through <term>putrefaction</term> <note>The stage of breaking down substances, often associated with the color black.</note> at the bottom of the appropriate vessel—that is, in the <term>alembic</term> and the <term>circulatory cucurbit</term> <note>Types of glass distillation apparatus.</note>, which are beautifully expressed by the two birds bound together and devouring each other's tails. 
<margin><unclear>Blackness</unclear> <unclear>Whiteness</unclear></margin>For in this vessel, the water—digested and purified by its own spirit—emerges from the prison of darkness and the kingdom of blackness, and will finally turn into the <term>white earth</term>, the completion of the work.

<margin>The second part of the Chemical table.</margin>There follows the other part of the table of the three Suns joined by two rays, which nevertheless agrees with the previous part of the table and explains the <term>foliated water</term> <note>original: "aqua foliata"; a term for the "Philosopher's Gold" or a purified mercurial state.</note>, which is the Gold of the Philosophers and the life-giving cloud. It is threefold: like the Sun described as shining with two rays (the figure of two-in-one), and the Sun having one ray (the figure of one-in-one), which are the earth; for the water is composed of two natures. It is also called threefold because it is one thing in which there are three: namely fire, air, and water. The earth existing as black below is the <term>Lower World</term> mixed and tempered from the two, and the figure is of two-in-one—that is, composed of two bodies into one. It is explained by five things: a vessel like a full Moon, in whose belly the Moon is hidden; two rays; and a third ray descending from on high to the depths surrounding the earth. This earth is threefold: the first enters into their bodies; the second is the earth of the <term>Lunar work</term> and is the beginning of the second operation, making the red body of the Sun out of the white; the third earth, through the Sun placed below, marks the completion of the entire work. For the water poured over the black earth renders it white, which is followed (after the heat is increased) by the <term>rubification</term> <note>The "reddening" or final stage of the alchemical Great Work.</note>, the end and limit of the <term>Solar work</term>. For if you cast three portions of water upon the dissolved earth, as soon as it is dissolved it passes into one earth, with the water part swimming over it in the form of liquid pitch; all of this is performed by the slow fire of manure or ashes through putrefaction. 

Now, as for what they understand by the ten <margin><unclear>Eagles</unclear></margin>equipped with bows and arrows, receive this: Eagles are animals of an entirely fiery and very swift nature, sympathetic to Solar operations. They hint at the subtlety and penetrating power of the volatile spirits that intervene in this Hermetic work, which is rightly indicated by the bows and arrows. There are ten of them because the great work is finished by a tenfold operation performed with their help. I deliberately do not add the <term>Praxis</term> <note>The practical, hands-on laboratory instructions.</note>, since it can easily be established from what has been said above.

You have, therefore, the solution to the Enigma, which, although it tastes of something Egyptian, has been corrupted by the Arabs and [differs] somewhat from the genuine...

# CLASS IX. HIEROGLYPHIC MEDICINE. 423 CHAPTER VI.

<margin>A chemical Hermetic Hieroglyph, and its explanation.</margin>
...deviated from its own purity; in order to restore it, let us subjoin in this place a Hermetic hieroglyph, the interpretation of which will perhaps shed greater light than the previous one. It was, moreover, sent to me from Egypt, and transcribed from a most celebrated stone at Cairo—which they call the "shell of love"—by Michael Schatt of Memphis; and it is as follows. The "shell of love" denotes a chemical vessel <note>likely a retort or flask</note> in which, while sympathetic substances are placed within, they are joined in perfect love once their contraries have been put to flight, as the symbols to be explained shortly hereafter teach. A figure of Anubis, a man sitting on a throne, pressing two crocodiles under his feet, holds a lion and serpents in his right hand, and scorpions and a dog in his left; below is placed a serpent in an undulating coil devouring its own tail; nearby stands a man <term>appearing like fire <note>original Greek: pyreknomorphos</note></term> striking a hippopotamus with a spear; on the other side is a man in the form of an Ibis leading a hippopotamus; between them mediates a dragon-shaped butterfly. By Anubis, no other is meant but Hermes or Mercury, whom they commonly represent with a dog's head to indicate his supreme sagacity in searching out the secrets of nature, and thus Mercury himself is pointed out. He sits on a throne to indicate the power both of Mercury and of the other secrets of the lower world shining forth in the inner recesses of nature, <margin>See the figure on page 259 of Volume II, Part II.</margin> which he was investigating. He presses two crocodiles with his feet; these are indeed none other than the Typhonian spirits <note>referring to Set/Typhon, representing chaos or corrosive forces</note> which lie hidden in metals—sharp, biting, poisonous, and corroding all things; indeed, unless these are suppressed, you will achieve nothing worthy in the Art <note>Alchemy</note>. With his right hand he holds a lion by the tail, which resists and tends by a certain sympathetic force toward the Ibis-shaped figure, which is the Mercurial force. The "Chemical Lion" is the gold of the Philosophers, which is carried toward Mercury by a certain natural attraction of inclination, seeking its friendship with the greatest ardor; when this has been done, Mercury is joined to the earth through a coagulating force, which is indeed aptly represented by the Ibis-shaped figure bound to the hippopotamus. For the hippopotamus is an amphibious animal and denotes earthy humidity; this is bound by Mercury, who nevertheless cannot entirely consume its extreme moisture; hence he calls the <term>one appearing like fire</term> to his aid—that is, a certain fiery force lying hidden in the center of the matter, by which the hippopotamus is fixed, once the corroding and poisonous spirits lurking in the Mercurial water have been put to flight. The dragon devours its own tail, that is, a return is made to a firm and solid substance through perfect fixation, and the "vegetated stone" acquires life for the intended multiplication; this is signified by the serpents which he holds in his hands.

<margin>An objection against the given explanation and its solution.</margin>
Someone will perhaps say: how can these things be applied to chemical matters, when these same figures have already been frequently applied to divine and theological matters? I respond that it is true, as we have also demonstrated throughout this work, that hieroglyphs acquire different senses, but according to the analogy of the Worlds, they are analogical; <margin>The same hieroglyph has different meanings.</margin> so that, for example, what is appropriate for the Archetypal Sun can be equally applied to the Sidereal, Medical, Chemical, and Ethical Sun. The Egyptians placed the only difference in this: that the secret doctrine of the hieroglyphs maintained a certain respect for the subject upon which it was inscribed. Thus, those inscribed on Obelisks denoted the highest and most sublime things proper to their Theology; but on Mummies, they denoted a favorable transmigration of souls <note>original: metempsychosis</note>;

# CHAPTER VI. THE EGYPTIAN GYMNASIUM OF HIEROGLYPHS

Thus, the ingenuity of the Egyptians is worthy of the highest praise, because they twisted one and the same symbol into so many various senses and meanings according to the diversity of the subjects upon which it was engraved. Therefore, the preceding symbol placed on an Obelisk displayed not a chemical meaning, but a Theological one hidden in the archetype of divinity; and so it is for the rest. I wished to warn the reader of this matter here first, lest the mind be rendered doubtful and perplexed by the aforementioned confusion of symbols. <margin>A third chemical enigma from Haled.</margin>
Furthermore, **Haled** <note>referring to Khalid ibn Yazid, an Umayyad prince and famous early alchemist</note> brings forward another comparison in the manner of an Enigma, to denote the preparation of the Hermetic work <note>the "Great Work" of alchemy</note> used by the Egyptians. This Enigma was translated from the Arabic idiom into Latin; it begins thus:

> *There is a land among us called Tormus, in which certain reptiles stable themselves, which eat opaque things from burning stones, and in this way they drink the blood of black goats; remaining in the Shadow, they conceive in baths, give birth in the air, walk upon the sea, and remain in monuments and tombs; and the reptile fights against its male, and in the tomb its male remains for forty nights, and in the small house for forty nights, until they come forth like white doves; and each shall cast its seed upon the marble into an image, and flying crows shall come, and having made an attack upon it, rushing down they collect it; then they fly above the peaks of mountains, and there, having been whitened, they sprout and bring forth manifold offspring.*

And this is the Arabic Enigma, by which they aptly indicate the process of the entire art. But let us explain the individual parts.

<margin>Explanation of Haled's Enigma.</margin>
All these things are said to happen in the land of **Tormos**, that is, of lupines <note>original: "lupinorum"; likely a pun or code for a specific chemical base</note>; but by the land of lupines, they understand the "first matter" <term>Materia Prima: the raw, unrefined base material used in alchemy</term> of the Hermetic art. In this land, serpents and reptiles are nourished, which eat opaque things from burning stones and drink the blood of black goats. The reptiles are the metallic, saline, Mercurial, and Arsenical spirits; corrosive, eating, and dissolving the opaque things—that is, the metallic matter under which they lie hidden. They are watered by the blood of black goats, which refers to a tinging and fertile watery substance, aptly hinted at by the blood of black goats; for just as the goat, a lustful animal, enters the female at any time, so the stone, when it joins with the female in the Hermetic preparation, is blackened after its whitening by the power of the philosophical fire. Thus it conceives in baths and gives birth in the air; that is, as soon as it is enclosed in the gourd <note>original: "cucurbita," a round-bottomed flask</note>, it lays the rudiments of its first conception, but it gives birth to the conceived offspring by the power of fire elevated into the chamber of the alembic <note>the "alembic" is the cap or still-head used for distillation</note>—that is, in the air. For the vapor, dissolved into water in the air of the alembic's chamber, is collected in the receiver, which is "walking upon the sea," where it dwells as if in a tomb, where the enclosed spirits begin a new battle. The reptile fights against its male for forty nights; that is, it attacks the imperfections lurking in the prepared matter, by corroding them and consuming them through various purifications for the time defined by chemists. When these are consumed and purified, the long-desired whiteness finally [appears] through white doves...

<margin>Hermes.</margin>
Hence Hermes rightly says: let the water of the matter be gently raised from the earth to the heaven, and it acquires power from the higher things, and descends into the earth, and has in itself the virtue of the superior and the inferior, and it has the light of lights, and therefore darkness flees from it.
