<margin>
How the sanctuaries were adorned, and what was done in them.
</margin>
We have dealt copiously with the inner sanctuaries <note>original: *adyta*, the most private, "un-enterable" parts of a temple</note> of the Egyptians—those dark and subterranean places—in Volume I, Treatise V. Therefore, it only remains to explain in this place what the Magi worked within them, and what ceremonies they performed. There were, moreover, many hiding places of this kind in Egypt, and as Clement <note>Clement of Alexandria, a Christian theologian who wrote extensively on Egyptian customs</note> says, there were shrines of diabolical arts according to the number of Oracles or Districts <note>original: *Nomorum*, the administrative divisions of ancient Egypt</note>. In these, first, the documents of hieroglyphic doctrine were seen depicted on the walls, most fit for attracting spirits. The primary Deity, with attendant Spirits <note>original: *Genijs*</note> differing according to the nature of the place, was seen placed upon an altar, deformed by a strange transformation. There was also a nearby sacred pool, destined for the use of rites and expiations. The whole place was dark, and could only be illuminated by lights. Within this, the Priests assembled on appointed days, in that habit of clothing and ornament in which both the primary Deity and the attendants were seen adorned. In the highest silence, they bore witness to those shadows of the supreme and immense Deity, which were indicated by the gloom of the place. Then, they taught those about to be initiated into the sacred rites the mysteries, power, and efficacy of the individual figures depicted on the walls—a fragment of which the most learned Nardius <note>Giovanni Nardi, a Florentine physician and scholar</note> sent to me not long ago, as will be seen later. Indeed, the reasoning of these things was held in such high esteem among the Greek Philosophers (even if reported only by rumor) that, as Clement testifies: <margin>Clement.</margin> *Pythagoras was circumcised, so that having descended into the inner sanctuaries, he might learn the mystical philosophy from the Egyptians* <note>original Greek: ὁ Πυθαγόρας περιτέμνετο, ἵνα δὴ καὶ εἰς τὰ ἄδυτα κατελθὼν τὴν μυστικὴν παρ' Αἰγυπτίων ἐκμάθῃ φιλοσοφίαν</note>; <margin>Justin Martyr.</margin> and Justin in *Questions to the Orthodox*, chapter 25: *At that time, the hieroglyphic disciplines, as they are called, which were given in the inner sanctuaries and in carvings, were held in honor among the Egyptians; but they were handed down only to those [chosen] ones. Astronomy and astrology among them at that time were considered common, pedestrian, and marketplace subjects.* <note>original Greek: Τίμια δὲ καὶ ποτὲ παρ' Αἰγυπτίοις μαθήματα τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ καλούμενα τὰ ἐν τοῖς ἀδύτοις καὶ τοῖς τυπέσι· ἀλλὰ τοῖς ἐκείνοις παραδιδόμενα, ἀστρονομία δὲ καὶ ἀστρολογία παρ' αὐτοῖς τοτε χυδαῖα τε καὶ πεζὰ, καὶ ἀγοραῖα μαθήματα ἐλογίζετο.</note> At that time, the hieroglyphic disciplines were in high value among the Egyptians, which were given in the sanctuaries to any of the most select, not to men from the crossroads <note>i.e., common people</note>. <margin>By what rites the Priests petitioned.</margin> But Astrology was cast down, being itinerant and vulgar among them. # CLASS XI. HIEROGLYPHIC MAGIC. CHAPTER V.

To consecrate the use of Oracles <note>Latin: *Oraculorum vsum*</note>; then, after the ceremonies mentioned a little earlier, the Priest—who, according to Apuleius in his *Apology*, was required to be properly skilled in the laws of ceremonies, the divine law of sacred rites, and the justice of religions—would begin. And as Libanius says in his 43rd declamation: <margin>Lucian.</margin> *To know the positions of the Gods, and their secrets, and in what things they rejoice, and by what they are offended, and what they might give back in return for what they receive* <note>original Greek: *Ἐπίστασθαι θεῶν θέσεις...*</note>; with a horrid murmur and imperious words, as Lucian testifies in his *Dialogues of the Dead* <note>Latin: *Necricis*</note>, he twists the gods above and the spirits of the dead. A harmful song is surrounded by brass, then with shivering words a covered urn is shut tight, and thrice nine times he murmurs a song with a magical mouth. 

But even this is done with a great difference, for they do not always use threats or the utterance of portentous words. For when they supplicated the Supreme Deity and the choir of the Supreme Powers, they did so only through hymns, songs, sacrifices, and a previous disposition and expiation of the soul and body, freed from all the filth of earthly contagion. <margin>The Egyptian Priests sought Deification.</margin> By this they intended nothing other than *Deification* <note>original Greek: *ϑεωσίαν* (theosian), meaning transformation into God</note>, which, once they had attained it—being then worthy of the company of the Gods—they believed there was no power so great that they could not command it and make it subject to their own law. 

However, they did use threats against a certain genus of demons of an inferior order, which they compelled to do what they wished through imperious and threatening words. So says Iamblichus. His words are: <margin>Porphyry.</margin> Porphyry relates that the Priests were accustomed to use certain violent threats against the Powers Above. <margin>The Egyptian Priests threatened the Gods.</margin> These threats were generally: *Unless you do so, or conversely, if you do something, I shall shatter the heavens, or I shall disclose the secrets of Isis, or I shall divulge the mystery hidden in the abyss, or I shall scatter the sacred Chest-boat* <note>Latin: *Cistam barin*, referring to the sacred solar bark or processional boat</note> *—that is, a certain ship sacred among the Egyptians—or the limbs of Osiris to Typhon* <note>Typhon is the Greek name for Set, the antagonist of Osiris</note>*, and other similar things.* 

All of which <margin>Psellus:</margin> Psellus, in his book *On the Operation of Demons*, chapter 21, confirms when he says: [All kinds of demons are wonderfully bold and yet timid. Especially those which are *thick* <note>Greek: *παχύλα* (pachyla), referring to "gross" or material spirits</note> or affected by matter. Indeed, the aerial ones, in whom there is much cleverness, if someone rebukes them, they cannot discern who is rebuking them; nor can anyone be freed from their vexation except he who worships God with holiness of life and, relying on divine power, chants the tremendous name of the Word of God. 

But these demons, namely those affected by matter, fearing lest they be banished into the abysses and subterranean passages, and fearing the Angels who banish them there—when someone threatens that they will be banished thither and expresses the names of the Angels to whom that duty is assigned—it can hardly be said with what great fear and disturbances they are shaken. For they are so struck in spirit that they cannot even discern who the one threatening them is; whether an old woman or a little old man expresses such threats, so great a fear then invades them that they mostly depart, as if those who threaten them were also able to put them to death; to such an extent are they timid, nor do they know how to discern anyone. Therefore, they are most easily tamed by that impure kind of Enchanters using excremental things—I mean saliva, nails, and hair—and being bound with wax and a thin thread, they avoid those tragic afflictions and disturbances through those cursed exorcisms and abjurations.] What, however, through this kind of...

# CHAPTER V. 454 EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

I have decided that the way they wished to indicate the threats of the gods, or how they were able to command the Gods, must be explained according to the Egyptian mindset.

<margin>The Egyptians thought that certain Spirits feared men who were "seized by God" <note>original: Θεολήπτας (Theoleptas). This refers to individuals in a state of divine possession or religious ecstasy.</note></margin>
It must therefore be understood that in the World, according to the hieroglyphic doctrine of the Priests, there is a certain class of Powers that reveres and fears those men who are "seized by God" and who, through the continuous exercise of sacred rites, have been transformed into a certain divine essence. These Powers, struck with awe, obey their commanding words—not indeed by human strength, but by the divine power of the ineffable sacraments. For as Iamblichus <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher (c. 245–325 AD) who wrote extensively on theurgy and Egyptian mysteries.</note> rightly says, since a Priest of this kind is established in the order of the higher Gods, he therefore employs commands and threats appropriate to a nature greater than his own. Yet he does not do this as if he were actually going to perform what he then asserts, but rather to declare how much power he has obtained through his union with the Gods, arising from his knowledge and possession of ineffable symbols and seals.

<margin>Iamblichus. <unclear>On the Mysteries, ch. 6. ...</unclear></margin>
Iamblichus notes another reason as well for the obedience of the Demons <note>In this context, "Demons" (Dæmones) refers to intermediary spirits or guardians of the natural order, not necessarily evil entities.</note> to the threatening voices of the Priests: for there are some Demons divided among the provinces and parts of the World, each destined for the continuous guardianship of the things committed to their faith. These have such great care for the things entrusted to them that they cannot tolerate even a word contrary to that order and dispensation; for no other reason than that the order of the Gods persists in them by a constant and unshakable law of necessity, free from all change, which they guard with a worldly perseverance. Therefore, these terrestrial Demons, just as they live within the things committed to their faith and draw their being from them, so they do not permit those very things—so closely related and dear to them—to be attacked by such torments as threats; indeed, they cannot even bear to hear them, because they understand that the order and even the disposition of the entire Universe is chiefly contained within those mysteries, which are the very Divinities indicated allegorically through words.

<margin>Threats intended for the Demons by the Egyptians: what they signify.</margin>
Therefore, when they say, "I shall shatter the Heavens," or "I shall reveal the secrets of Isis," or "I shall divulge the mystery hidden in the abyss," or "I shall scatter the *baris* <note>A Greek word for an Egyptian boat; here referring to a sacred ritual vessel or the solar bark.</note> or the limbs of Osiris to Typhon" <note>Typhon is the Greek name for Set, the god of chaos who dismembered Osiris.</note>—since this would be repugnant to the order of the whole, and consequently contrary to the order of their guardianship—they are disturbed by this. To prevent such things from being set in motion further, they condescend to the will of the priests. For the parts of the World remain in order for no other reason than that the beneficent power of Osiris, pure and untouched, cannot be mixed or confounded by any contrary tumult or error. Furthermore, the life of all things persists as pure and incorruptible because the whole World endures by an eternal law through the life-giving and harmonic principles hidden within Isis. For who could restrain the course of the Sun and Moon? Who could open the abysses? Who could delay the *baris*, that is, the vehicle of the World's principles? Lest the order of nature be changed and undergo a contrary fate, they do not wish those things to be profaned by threatening words—things which, by the gift of the eternal Gods, have obtained a lot free from all contrariety and perpetual instability. Let these things said according to the mind of the Egyptians suffice. I shall add in this place a fragment sent by the most learned Nardi, of whom we made mention above on page 452.

...of white marble with hieroglyphics, which was sent to me not long ago for interpretation by that most learned man, Thomas Henshaw, an Englishman <note>Thomas Henshaw (1618–1700) was an English diplomat and a charter member of the Royal Society.</note>. The stone is white, much softer than marble, and undoubtedly from the subterranean crypts of Egypt, where hieroglyphics were most commonly carved into softer stones of this kind, as they were properly protected there from all damage by the air. The height of the stone is three feet minus one inch; the width is one foot and 2 1/2 inches. The thickness is about 4 1/4 inches. The upper figures are 1 foot 5 inches high. The lower ones are 8 inches each, containing spaces of 2 inches. The space which is empty below the figures contains one foot, according to English measurements. The stone is curved at the top, and with the rest of its frame it seems to represent a sanctuary; in the top of which you see a winged globe marked with the letter D, below which various small hieroglyphic characters (which, however, have been corroded by the injury of time so that what they represent cannot be known) are carved into the walls. Below these is seen the figure of a naked man, **A**, crowned with an Egyptian headdress <note>original: "cidari Ægyptia"</note>, in a sitting posture; he holds a whip in his right hand and a staff in the other. Behind his back is a female image, **B**, wrapped in a linen garment down to her ankles; from her head, which is adorned with a veil and ribbons, emerges a serpent-bearing globe, appearing to anxiously seek something from figure **A**. On the other side, figure **C** is seen, naked from the navel to the top of the head, in male attire, with arms outstretched and fingers seemingly turning into serpents. Between figures **A** and **C** an altar is placed, equipped with a cone-shaped vessel and two small globes.

<margin>Interpretation of the Sistrum <note>The sistrum was a sacred rattle used in Egyptian ritual.</note>.</margin>

I shall now explain what these things indicate. The winged globe signifies the providence of the Supreme Divinity pervading all things. Figure **A** denotes Osiris, the Solar Deity and the "Averter of Evil" <note>original Greek: ἀποτομαῖον (apotomaion)</note>; this is sufficiently shown by the whip, the scepter, the sitting posture, and the headdress, which are symbols of supreme lordship and power. He is depicted naked because the Divinity is immune to any mixture of earthly contagion. To him is joined Isis, **B**, the Moon, the inseparable companion of Osiris, as shown by the globe resting on her head adorned with the horned face of the Moon, and by the veil and ribbons. She is wrapped in a linen garment to indicate that her nature is difficult to investigate. With her arm raised, she seems to demand the commands of Osiris, ready to execute whatever he orders. Figure **C** denotes a small sacrificer or a Priest of the Mysteries <note>term: Hieromantem - a priest who explains sacred mysteries</note> who adjures Osiris. He is naked to signify that no one is fit for the company of the Gods who has not first withdrawn his mind from all contagion of human affairs. He has his arms raised in a gesture of prayer; his fingers end in something resembling serpents, by which apt symbol they note that the operations of Priests ought to be full of life and spirit so that they may become participants in the gifts of the Gods. He is bald because hair is the excrement of bodily filth and a hiding place for animals <note>likely referring to lice</note>, from which the initiate of the sacred rites, a companion of the Gods, must be purged. The table equipped with vessels indicates that without rites and ceremonies, all attraction and soothing of the Gods is vain and fleeting; for these are the incitements of the Gods, by which—when the prior disposition of the Prophets is added—they finally become masters of their prayers. The Hieroglyphic schemes distinguished below in a triple order signify those things by which...

## CHAPTER VI.

### *Concerning the amulet-magic of the Gnostics, and the Ephesian letters, which are the first branch of Egyptian Magic.*

<margin>The first branch of Egyptian Magic. The amulet-magic of the Gnostics.</margin>
<margin>The Gnostic Masters were followers of Egyptian impieties.</margin>
It is well known that most of the leaders of that school—who were Christians in name only, having long ago sworn themselves to the words of the Master Devil—were Egyptian by birth. That these followers of Gnostic impiety revived the abominable superstitions, rites, and ceremonies of the ancient Egyptians from the underworld, with the Devil as their initiator <note>original: "mystagogo"</note>, is witnessed by their abominable sacrifices, magical arts, and other cursed crimes. For these, see the works of Epiphanius, Irenaeus, Philastrius, Augustine, Tertullian, and Theodoret <note>These are Church Fathers who wrote extensively against early Christian heresies.</note>. Among the Gnostics, those most infamous for these abominations are recorded as Marcus the Egyptian Magician, Basilides the master of luxury, and Carpocrates the defender of filthy dogma; also Valentinus and Cerinthus, cultivators and followers of Egyptian rites and superstitions.

<margin>Why the Gnostics were so named.</margin>
<margin>Epiphanius. Nicephorus.</margin>
The Gnostics wished to be so called because of the "excellence of knowledge" <note>Greek: gnosis</note> which they boasted; they were also called *Borborites* <note>original: "βορβορεί" (borborei), meaning "miry" or "filthy" ones.</note> as if "muddy," on account of the excessive vileness, foulness, and horrific, abominable turpitude they were said to practice in their sacred rites. Epiphanius describes these rites vividly in Book 1, Volume 2; consult him there. Nicephorus also writes about them in Book 4, Chapter 2 of his *Ecclesiastical History* in these words: *"And indeed, Irenaeus, likewise dealing with Basilides, brings his shameful error into the open; he reports that Carpocrates was his equal, the author and leader of those called Gnostics. He was not ashamed to openly practice a magical life, which his father Simon <note>Referring to Simon Magus.</note> had professed secretly and craftily; he hunted for glory and exalted himself through curious arts, through the 'loves' <note>likely referring to love-charms or philters</note> which he fashioned, through dream-visions, and through attendant demons."* These men, therefore, raising the Egyptian superstitions (of which they boasted they were the heirs) from the underworld, infected the entire East with them. For, insisting upon their erroneous dogmas, they established a new art of signs <note>original: "characteristicam artem"</note> by which they fashioned various amulets. These were engraved on various stones according to the nature and property of the Divinity they invoked through them, circumscribed with ancient Egyptian characters, and marked with the names of powerful Angels, placed according to the prescriptions of hieroglyphic laws.

<margin>Amulets of the Gnostics</margin>
By these means, they boasted they could perform wonders. From among their number, out of countless examples, a few follow, in which you will find everywhere Harpocrates sitting on a Lotus, Isis, Serapis, Hecate, and other Divinities—or more truly, monsters—of the Egyptians.

The figure marked with the number 17 is a hawk-shaped asp <note>original: "Aspis ἱερακόμορφος"</note>, such as frequently occurs on the Bembine Tablet <note>The Bembine Tablet is a famous bronze plate with Egyptian-style motifs, popular among Renaissance occultists</note>; it is a Roman invention fashioned in the likeness of the Egyptians, as the Latin letters L, I, and S show, and they signify the same as "Liberty preserved" or "the safety of the children." 18 is a hawk-shaped Osiris, carrying a basket on his head, holding in his right hand a staff shaped like a hoopoe bird <note>original: "Cucucomorphū"</note> with a staff of office and a sundial pointer <term>gnomon: the part of a sundial that casts a shadow</term>, and in his left hand carrying a handled cross <note>original: "Crucem ansatam," referring to the Ankh</note> in a forked shape. This denotes the Solar Deity, signified by the hawk's head, as we have already frequently taught from the writings of Eusebius. He carries the basket on his head as a symbol of the abundance which he provides; the scepter marked with the head of a hoopoe <note>original: "Gucuphæ"</note> denotes the variety of things he produces; the staff of office denotes harmony; the sundial pointer denotes the symmetry of things which he establishes in the world; the handled cross, which he carries in his left hand, denotes the diffusion of the Solar spirit through all things. 19 is a twisted serpent, marked with two horns, signifying the same as 17. 20 and 5 are hawk-shaped amulets of Osiris, between which is placed a coin marked with a Lion on one side and a numerical table <note>original: "abaco numerico," a magic square</note> on the other. It shows that it was minted with the Sun entering Leo, in order to attract the Solar Deity HELOY <note>A Greek-derived name for the Sun/God</note>, as the character of the Sun and the Lion itself teaches. The numerical table is dedicated to the Sun, whose Intelligence they call Raphael; it is nothing other than the square of the number six, so skillfully arranged that each series of numbers—vertical, horizontal, and diagonal—when joined together produces the same sum. But since this figure has been most fully explained in our *Hieroglyphic Arithmetic*, we refer the reader there. Δ <note>original: alchemical symbol for fire</note> denotes the fiery triangle. Note, reader, that this coin is not ancient, but was devised by later astrologers. There follows another coin from the same period, on the front face of which is Jupiter sitting, formidable with a lightning bolt, near whom is the Jovial Eagle and his character ♃, whose name in the Cabala is Zadkiel <insert>צדקיאל</insert>; for the Hebrews call Jupiter *Tzedek* <insert>צדק</insert>, that is, the judge of justice. Here, "Satquiel" is corruptly written for Zadkiel. Above Jupiter, the figure of Sagittarius is placed, which indicates that this coin of thundering Jupiter was minted when the Sun was positioned in Sagittarius. The back part displays a table composed of Hebrew letters, and indicates nothing other than the square of the number four (16), arranged with such skill that the individual numbers indicated by the letters, when joined in any series, produce the same sum. We have taught in our *Arithmetic* that the square of four was sacred to Jupiter, where you will find everything explained at length. From what has just been said, it clearly shines forth that the Gnostics learned all these fanatical delusions from the Egyptians, if the Reader rightly compares them with the Egyptian Amulets placed just before. Furthermore, the names—confused and corrupted from the Egyptian and Hebrew languages—manifest this sufficiently. It is characteristic of scoundrels of this sort to use these barbarous names, which resound with hissing and growling, to stun the ears of those attending their wicked rites, simultaneously inspiring horror and conciliating authority for their mysteries. Irenaeus beautifully teaches this in Book 1, *On the Errors of the Gnostics*, and Nicetus derives it at length from Irenaeus.

> In order to strike greater amazement, says Nicetus (following Irenaeus), into the one being baptized, they add these Hebrew names: [*Besama, camosi, bne, anoora, mystadia, rhuda, custaba, phogor, calathi*], the interpretation of which is this: *O you who are above every power of the father, we invoke you, who are called light and good Spirit, and life, because you have reigned in the body.*

Thus says Nicetus. To confess the truth, it is very difficult to indicate the sources of those words; for no trace of the Hebrew language appears under them, except in a very corrupted form, as in *besama* <term>in the spice <note>Hebrew: בסמא (be-sama)</note></term>, *camosi* <term>my hidden ones <note>Hebrew: כמוסי (kamusi)</note></term>, *phogor* <term>opening/gap <note>Hebrew: פגור (pagur), likely a corruption of Peor</note></term>, nor any Chaldean—

### Ephesian Letters.

<margin>
What the Ephesian letters are, and of what sort.
</margin>

The Ephesian letters were *magical spells* <note>original Greek: "μαγευματα"</note> or incantations, by which, through the utterance of certain barbarian and portentous names, they either purified infested places, or drove away diseases, or adjured Demons. They are called "Ephesian" because they were first invented at Ephesus by the Idaean Dactyls <note>Mythical ancient craftsmen and magicians</note>, and were engraved upon the statue of Diana of the Ephesians. Thus Clement in Book 1 of the *Stromata* and Plutarch in his *Symposiacs* mention them in these words: <note>original Greek: "ὥσπερ δαιμονιζομένους μάγοι κελεύουσι τὰ Ἐφέσια γράμματα πρὸς αὑτοὺς καταλέγειν καὶ ὀνομάζειν."</note>

<margin>
Clement.
Plutarch.
</margin>

> Over those possessed by Demons, the Magicians ordered the Ephesian letters to be recited and named.

Diogenianus <note>A Greek grammarian and collector of proverbs</note> supports this: *The Ephesian letters*, he says, *are certain incantations, which those who spoke them were victorious in everything.* <note>original: "Ἐφέσια γράμματα... ἐπῳδαί τινές εἰσι"</note> Moreover, Hesychius <margin>Hesychius</margin> records that the following names were composed from these Ephesian letters: *Aski, kataski, aix, tetrax, damnameneus, aision.* He explains that *aski* signifies darkness, *kataski* light, *aix* the self <note>or "the goat" in literal Greek, though interpreted here as a primary force</note>, *damnameneus* the Sun, and *aision* the truth. *Aski Cataski hex, tetrax damnameneus, aesion.* And indeed *Aski* signifies the same as *darkness*, *Cataski* the same as *light*, *hex* the same as "itself," *damnameneus* as the *Sun*, and *aesion* as the *truth*.

<margin>Zonaras</margin>
As Zonaras <note>A Byzantine chronicler</note> relates in his account of Constantine the Great, Zambres the Hebrew whispered these words into the ear of a bull and it immediately dropped dead; later, Pope Sylvester <margin>Clement</margin> raised it back to life in the name of Christ. Clement of Alexandria reports the aforementioned words slightly differently; for in Book 5 of the *Stromata* <note>"Miscellanies," a work of early Christian philosophy</note> he speaks thus: *Androcides the Pythagorean certainly says that the letters called "Ephesian" hold the place of symbols; he says that "askion" signifies darkness, because it has no shadow; "kataskion" signifies light, since it illuminates the shadow; "aix" is the ancient name for the earth; and "tetrax," that is, the quaternary, signifies the year because of the seasons; "damnameneus" is the Sun, because it tames all things; and "aisia" is the true voice. The symbol signifies that the order of divine things is like darkness when compared with light, the Sun compared with the year, and the earth compared with every kind of natural generation.*

<margin>Barbarous words with which Branchus the seer purified the Milesians.</margin>
From this same storehouse proceeded the "barbarous names" <term>barbara nomina: foreign or unintelligible words used in magic for their perceived power</term> with which Branchus the Seer is said to have purified the Milesians from famine; for he, sprinkling the multitude with laurel branches, led them in singing a hymn in this manner:

->Sing, boys, "bens, becaergon," and "becaergam."<-

Then the people cried out: *Bedy, Zaps, Chton, Plectrum, Sphinx, Cnachzbi, Chrypotes, Phlegmo, Drops*. And *Bedy* indeed, according to Clement, signifies water; *Zaps* the sea; *Chton* the earth; *Plectrum* the Sun; *Sphinx* the ether or the framework of the World; *Cnachzbi* milky nourishment; and finally *Drops* signifies the effective word. All those portentous names uttered by the Magi can be traced back to the Ephesian letters; and just as they were born in darkness and brought forth by "darkness-dwellers" <note>Latin: "tenebrioribus," a play on words for swindlers or those who shun the light</note> in the dark, so we leave them eternally buried in darkness as things unworthy of the light.

# CHAPTER VII.

<margin>The second branch of Egyptian Magic.</margin>
## II. The Branch of Egyptian Magic.

### Section I.

->*Concerning the Magic of the Hebrews, Arabs, and other peoples; containing various species of divination: Geomancy <note>divination by earth or dots</note>, Alectryomancy <note>divination by a rooster picking grain</note>, and Arithmomancy <note>divination by numbers</note>, and the Pythagorean Kabbalah; in which the supreme deceits and crafts of Satan in entangling the souls of mortals are revealed.*<-

Since the Hebrews, by the force of their Law, were strictly forbidden from seeking responses from sculpted Oracles, they strove with great zeal to procure them in another way: namely, by changing sensible images into the elements of letters. To ensure the fraud was not detected, these were for the most part transcribed from the Sacred Books; it is incredible how many souls they lost under the pretext of religion. <margin>The origin of characteristic magic.</margin> For this is the rightful origin of all "characteristic magic" <note>magic using signs or symbols</note>, Grammatomancy <note>divination by letters</note>, as well as the Pythagorean Kabbalah, as will be discussed later. And just as the Devil acts as God’s ape in all things, so he took the very argument for perverting souls through new superstitions from the Holy Scriptures themselves. For as we explained in the section on the Kabbalah of the Hebrews, they scrutinized the Sacred Letters for the names, virtues, and effects of foreign Angels; these they marked with the name of God, believing them to possess great powers to rescue men from any evils whatsoever. But concerning these, see the cited Class on the Kabbalah. <margin>The Hebrew divining wheel made of Hebrew letters.</margin> Furthermore, since they saw that Hebrew letters were so arranged that in whatever way they were joined, or by whatever combination they were transposed, they always exhibited some meaning; from this they organized a divining wheel, by the revolution of which they practice innumerable superstitions. <margin>Pardes <note>likely referring to the Pardes Rimmonim by Moses Cordovero</note>.</margin> This was performed, according to the witness of Pardes, in the following manner. They cut four circles of different sizes out of the cleanest parchment, all easily rotatable upon a central axis. Each of these was divided into twenty-two parts, and by lines drawn from the center to the circumference, four Hebrew alphabets were inscribed in the spaces of the four circumferences. On the outer fixed rim, there was an extended hand, on whose index finger the <term>Tetragrammaton</term> <note>the four-letter name of God, YHWH</note> was seen inscribed; and thus the instrument was held ready. Those about to consult it regarding doubts would first, with preliminary actions (which I deliberately omit here), seem to pray to the Intelligence hidden therein to favor the divinatory work more earnestly. When these things were finished, they would all grasp the circle by the handles with both hands and, with eyes raised to heaven, spin it wherever chance might take it. When the motion ended, they observed the four letters shown by the hand in the space drawn from the center to the final circumference; for these four letters, combined among themselves, [gave] the response...

# CLASS XI. HIEROGLYPHIC MAGIC. CHAPTER VII

They considered the letters assigned to the grains that had been taken and gathered them into one to see what word they might show, and from this they then divined the matter in question. We read that the Sophist Libanius and Iamblichus <note>Libanius (c. 314–392 AD) was a Greek teacher of rhetoric; Iamblichus (c. 245–325 AD) was a Neoplatonist philosopher. Both were associated with traditional pagan practices during the rise of Christianity.</note> used this sortilege <term>sortilege: divination by drawing lots or random symbols</term> when they were divining who would be the successor to the Imperial crown after the Emperor Valens. For a rooster, placed within the said circle after four grains were taken, left the spaces of the letters **Th, E, O, D** <note>original: $\vartheta, \epsilon, o, \delta$</note> empty of grains. From this they gathered that Theodorus would succeed to the Empire of Valens; but they were deceived by a Demon, for the event shortly after taught otherwise, as it was not Theodorus, but Theodosius who occupied the Imperial throne. Zonaras <margin>Zonaras</margin> <note>Joannes Zonaras, a 12th-century Byzantine chronicler and theologian.</note> mentions this sortilege in his account of Valens in these words: <note>original Greek: Ἐν κόνει τέσσαρα εἴκοσι γράμματα γράψας...</note> *Twenty-four letters are written in the dust, and a grain of wheat is placed upon each of them; then a rooster is set in the middle after certain incantations have been chanted, and they observe from which elements <note>In this context, "elements" refers to the letters of the alphabet.</note> the rooster takes the grains, which when joined together are thought to indicate that which is sought;* and later: *They saw the rooster taking the grain in the Th, the one in the E, the one in the O, and the one in the D.* The distinguished author Cedrenus <margin>Cedrenus</margin> <note>Georgius Cedrenus, an 11th-century Byzantine historian.</note> also mentions this **Alectryomancy** <term>Alectryomancy: divination by observing a rooster pecking at grain scattered on letters of the alphabet</term> in these words: *Writing,* he says, *the 24 letters in the dust and placing a grain of wheat upon each letter, they released a rooster onto the letters. And the rooster took the grain in the Th; then the grain in the E, and the O, and finally the grain in the D. And thus the divination was doubtful and ambiguous.* Sozomenus <margin>Sozomenus</margin> <note>Salamanes Hermias Sozomenus, a 5th-century historian of the Christian Church.</note> confirms this in Book 6 of his *Ecclesiastical History*. He says they adorned a tripod made of laurel, and by invocations and the words they were accustomed to use, they caused the name of the future Emperor to appear through the gathered letters, which emerged according to individual elements by the artifice of the tripod and a rotating divination. However, while everyone gaped at Theodorus, the composition of elements, which in his name had proceeded as far as the letter D, deceived the philosophers. Socrates <margin>Socrates</margin> <note>Socrates Scholasticus, a 5th-century Greek Christian church historian.</note> says in Book 4, Chapter 19: *A Demon persuaded certain curious Magi to inquire through magical arts who would gain power after Valens: to those using the magical art, the Demon responded not openly, but in his usual ambiguous way, showing the four letters **Th, E, O, D**, saying the name of him who was to be Emperor began with these letters.*

Indeed, I find that the Egyptians employed dogs, cats, and similar animals for the divination of future events. For they believed that, following a preliminary invocation, a Demon would incite the animal to show that which was sought, and in a certain way determine the outcome; yet the Demon, being by his nature always fallacious and a liar, would wretchedly mock and deceive the interpreters under his usual ambiguous symbols.

# CHAPTER VII. 474 EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

## § II.

### Concerning the Kabbalistic Amulets commonly used at this time.

<margin>Kabbalistic Amulets.</margin>
The more recent Hebrews <note>Referring to post-biblical Jewish scholars and Kabbalists</note> have for some time now sold to the world a new kind of amulet. Under the pretext of using sacred words, they promise all manner of benefits to the unlearned and common folk—a practice that is certainly all the more dangerous because it appears holy at first glance. And since it is difficult for those not trained in this art to distinguish the false from the true, it seemed fitting, for the honor of the Divine Name and the benefit of the Holy Mother Church, to expose the highly subtle deceptions of these impostors in this place. Thus, if these items should ever fall into the hands of simpler people—as they frequently do—they may be able to discern whether they can use them with a clear conscience. I undertake this task all the more willingly because I have long been urged to do so by the tribunal of the Sacred Inquisition.

<margin>A pernicious booklet entitled *Shimmush Tehillim*, the Practical Use of the Psalms.</margin>
It should be known, therefore, that a certain booklet issued from the Satanic school of the Hebrews is frequently handled by the curious. It is entitled <term>Shimmush Tehillim<note>original: "שמוש תהלים" - A medieval manual describing the magical or medicinal use of specific Psalms.</note></term>, that is, the *Practical Use of the Psalms*. From this book, as if from a lethal spring, flow the streams of all superstitious arts. <margin>Examples of Kabbalistic Magic.</margin> Upon this book, as if upon a foundation, the entire fabric and structure of Kabbalistic amulets rests. For in this work, they extract certain letters of the divine names from individual Psalms, which they then inscribe upon various objects: stones, metals, roots, parchments prepared by the art of divination, and "Isiac" ribbons <note>Likely referring to linen bands or wrappings reminiscent of Egyptian ritual bandages</note>. These amulets they sometimes wear on different parts of the body, sometimes give to animals to swallow, and sometimes cast into the elements to ward off the fury of fire, water, contagious air, or sterile earth. Just as these practices lack nothing in the way of superstition, they are rightly prohibited by the Holy Mother Church as soul-destroying and Satanic machinations, through which Satan, transforming himself into an angel of light, deceives and mocks mortals in various ways. Truly, he who desires to know such ravings more clearly should consult the aforementioned booklet *Shimmush Tehillim*, where he will discover the innumerable impostures of these idle Rabbis.

<margin>Crosses marked with Hebrew characters.</margin>
Of this same sort are certain Crosses brought from Spain, marked with various Hebrew characters and names. And truly, I cannot marvel enough at that frivolous persuasion—even among men thought to be very wise—by which they think something "great" lies hidden beneath such characters. For what has the Cross to do with these characters? If the Cross, sanctified by the touch of the Lord’s body, has great efficacy against Satanic temptations and for repelling the adversities of all evils, then surely the addition of letters and characters seems entirely superfluous. By their very nature, as has been shown throughout this work, they have absolutely no <margin>A coin marked with a pentagonal figure.</margin> efficacy. Also of this kind is that copper coin marked with a pentagonal figure <note>A pentagram or five-pointed star</note> and the sacred names of God, than which almost nothing is more common at this time. If you look only at the outer shell, it seems nothing but ho-

### §. III.

->Interpretation of the Cabalistic Coin.<-

<margin>Interpretation of the Cabalistic Coin.</margin>
<margin>The arts of the Devil in deceiving the unwary.</margin>
**H**ow thirstily the Demon of human perdition labors to ensnare men in his traps is something I believe no one can fail to gather from the various arts and means he uses everywhere in his machinations. Some he presses down by the weight of their own depraved nature; others he drives about as if by a whirlwind through the untamed violence of lusts and passions. Yet those whom the love of virtue or honesty invites to a holy and blameless life, he seeks to entangle through means suited to their own principles. Finally, he busies himself miserably ensnaring the simpler folk—who lack the prudent judgment to discern illusions—by transforming himself into an Angel of Light. Under a false cloak of divinity, he thrusts upon them impious things as holy, deceptions as miracles, and finally, magic incantations in place of divine prayers. This last method of temptation must be judged as much more dangerous than the others as it is more hidden and less understood by simple souls.

Among these provocations of the Devil, a primary place is held by those Cabalistic Phylacteries <note>term: Phylacteries; here referring to amulets or charms rather than the Jewish prayer boxes (tefillin)</note>, or magic scrolls, which the Hebrews call the Shields of David, or even the Seals of Solomon, marked with Hebrew names of both God and Angels. All of these, emerging from the workshop of Pluto <note>a classical reference to the ruler of the underworld, used here to mean Hell</note>, provide the ignorant common people with abundant material for errors and superstitions. This is especially true of this present Magic Coin, in which, if you consider the outer shell, you will find nothing at first glance that is not holy and divine; but if you examine the marrow, all is rotten, all is accursed. The coin is quite common, especially in Germany, France, and Italy, of the shape and size that follows:

<margin>The first face of the Coin.</margin>
This Cabalistic Coin <note>likely a "Jesus-medal" or a Renaissance-era talisman</note> has two figured faces: the first contains the figure of a pentagon inscribed within a circle; inscribed in the surrounding circle are these words:

*That is: And his name shall be called Wonderful, Counselor, Mighty God, Father of the future age, Prince of peace; and this name of mine, God our Just One shall call him; may his name be for eternity; before the face of this Sun let his name be spread.* Within the five triangles contained by the pentagon itself, five synonymous names attributed to Christ are contained, enclosed by three four-part circles; and in the first circle these names occur:

# CLASS XI. HIEROGLYPHIC MAGIC. 477 CHAPTER VII

In the names of the sacred titles appropriated to Christ, cursed blasphemies lie hidden, along with heresies and corruptions of the sacred text; for it is characteristic of Mages, through a pact entered into with the Demon, to conceal every kind of accursed thing under the veil of sacred names and figures, as an insult to Christ and the Saints. For they know that the Demon, cunning with the craft of a fox, will not cooperate in producing any effect except under this condition. And for that reason, Jewish sorcerers manufacture no amulet without these blasphemies against Christ being secretly inserted; just as formerly among the Pagans, almost no sacrifice was performed without human blood or shameful acts of lust: for the Devil rejoices in the contempt of God involved in such acts; once these are done, he promises he will grant anything. But concerning these matters, see the <term>Kabbalah</term> <note>A Jewish mystical tradition often misinterpreted or viewed with suspicion by Renaissance Christian scholars</note>; therefore, having dismissed those things, let us proceed with our explanation.

<margin>The Pentagram figure of the Kabbalistic Coin, called the Seal of Solomon.</margin>
And first indeed, so that the greater mysteries of this coin might appear, and so that the <term>Phylactery</term> <note>An amulet or charm worn for protection</note> might be more easily adopted by the superstitious for wicked use, they chose that common sign seen in the School of Mages: I mean that symbol of health, *Hygieia* <note>Greek: ὑγιεία, meaning health or wholeness</note>, which others also call the <term>pentalpa</term> <note>A five-pointed star formed by five interlocking Greek Alphas</note>. Agrippa, in Book 1 of *Occult Philosophy*, records that Antiochus, having placed this on his banner by the command of Alexander appearing to him in a dream, soon reported a wonderful victory over the Galatians. Therefore, just as those Greeks of old wore that symbol of health with the name *Hygieia* inscribed—adding the individual letters U, G, I, E, A <note>The letters of the Greek word for health</note> at the intervals of the corners—as an amulet; so the Hebrews inscribed various names appropriated to the Savior in the same pentagon, so that they might seem to have looked toward that Greek symbol of the pentalpha and its mysteries, while "hiding a black tail under a splendid garment" <note>A Latin idiom meaning to hide a sinister motive behind a fair appearance</note>.

-> [Image: A five-pointed star (pentagram) inside a circle. The Greek letters Υ, Γ, Ι, Ε, and Α are placed at the points.] <-

<margin>Blasphemies of the Kabbalistic Coin, called the Seal of Solomon.</margin>
And first indeed, in place of the circle they put the name *Yshu* <note>Hebrew: ישו</note>, as if it were a synonym for the others, *Yeshua* <note>Hebrew: ישוע</note>, *Yehoshua* <note>Hebrew: יהושוע</note>, etc. Yet it is so far from being a synonym for the name of JESUS that, on the contrary, nothing could be more opposed to it. For *Yshu* is not derived from *Ysha* <note>Hebrew: ישע</note>, which signifies "salvation," nor is it properly a Hebrew name, but was devised by the Hebrews as an insult to Christ from the capital letters of a certain sentence, which they call *Roshei Tevot* <note>Hebrew: ראשי תבות, meaning acronyms</note>. The sentence, or the words with which they are accustomed to curse any of the worst men, and from whose capital letters the name *Yshu* results, are these:

> *Yimmach Shemo Vezichro* <note>Hebrew: ימח שמו וזכרו</note>: that is: *May his name and memory be blotted out*.

And thus they are accustomed to curse Christ when they pronounce the name *Yshu*; who does not see how execrable a blasphemy this is?

<margin>Blasphemies of the Rabbis against Jesus Christ and Mary.</margin>
By a similar reasoning, they use other most holy mysteries of our faith—while they wish to mention them—for their contempt, using certain names devised in the stated manner or uttered equivocally. Thus, they call the Holy Gospel in Hebrew, out of contempt, *Auenzilion* <note>Hebrew: און גליון, a pun on 'Evangelion'</note>, that is, the *Volume of Iniquity*. Similarly, besides the fact that they call Christ *Thalui* <note>Hebrew: תלוי</note>, the *hanged one*, they also name the Blessed Virgin Mary *Thaluia* <note>Hebrew: תלויה</note>, that is, the *hanged woman*. But where they fear to call her so expressly for fear of Christians, they use circumlocution...

->Before the sun his name shall be propagated:<-

## § IV.

### Interpretation of another Cabalistic Heptagonal Amulet.

<margin>Interpretation of the heptagonal Cabalistic Amulet.</margin>
**T**his heptagonal <note>seven-sided</note> amulet enclosed in a circle is dedicated to Venus, as we have shown in *Hieroglyphic Arithmetic*. In the circumference are marked 72 letters extracted from the Cabala, each of which indicates one of the 72 Angels; concerning these, see the *Cabala of the Hebrews*, page 275. Who would not laugh at first sight at the stupidity of these idle men? While they have such faith in these Cabalistic follies—badly transformed into Latin letters—that they persuade themselves they can even move mountains by their help. But since the Devil, the enemy of the human race, does nothing except what results in an insult to Christ and the destruction of men; hence, to cover his Satanic wickedness, they industriously place the attributes of Christ on the corners of the heptagon—that is, the Angel of Darkness presents himself under the form of light. The attributes are as follows: Within the corner A B, inside a square, four letters are seen inserted into the individual angles of a Cross: **a.g.l.a.** This is a Hebrew name, and most celebrated in the Cabala, אגלא, which when expanded signifies the same as: *Atah Gibor Le-olam Adonai* <note>original: "אתה גבור לעולם אדני"</note> **"Thou art mighty forever, O Lord."** For if...

Finally, they inscribe a pentagon within this heptagon, in the center of which is the letter **T**, a symbol of salvation; around which, while they ought to have written these letters **HYGIEIA** <note>original: "υγιεια", Greek for "Health," a traditional Pythagorean greeting associated with the pentagram.</note>, being more ignorant than beasts, they substituted these: **e e ee y**. Within the triangles, however, from the amulet-making workshop of the Arabs, are placed **yl, al, le, al, um**, most corruptly like all the rest; for they wished to express that Arabic phrase **There is no god but God** <note>original: "لا اله الا الله" / "la alla ella alla"</note>, but since they were unable to pronounce it, they put those most awkward words in their place: **yl, al, le, al, um**. But as for what the two letters **um** mean, I shall explain. In the aforementioned Arabic pronouncement, "There is no god but God," these words always follow: **Muhammad is the messenger of God** <note>original: "محمد رسول الله" / "Mahumet raffulalla"</note>; and the capital letters of these refer to **um**. ...profess Muhammadanism; for in this single Amulet, a profession is made by those who carry it of four sects—Jewish, Christian, Muhammadan, and Pagan—and this is done through a secret pact with the Demon, instituted for that reason as an insult to the Christian religion. But I shall explain what the pentagon <note>The five-pointed star or pentagram</note> signifies. The Ancients, as we have taught in *Arithmetic*, dedicated the pentagon to Mars, just as they dedicated the heptagon <note>seven-sided figure</note> to Venus; by which they indicated that no one possesses Venus <note>love/pleasure</note> who has not first drawn near to Mars <note>war/struggle</note>; concerning which we have written more extensively in *Egyptian Astrology*. Therefore, whoever possesses an Amulet of this sort should persuade himself that he possesses something not natural, nor Divine or Angelic, but an immediate work of Diabolical machination, not to be used except with the eternal ruin of the soul.

# § V.

## *Explanation of another Magical Talisman.*

<margin>Thomas de Leon.</margin>
Father Thomas de Leon of our Society <note>The Jesuits</note>, Professor of Philosophy and Theology at Seville, and an eminent explorer of Oriental languages and the more abstruse learning of the Ancients, was the first to communicate this present Magical Talisman to me out of his affection for my studies. Indeed, just as he describes it diligently and skillfully in his letters sent to me, so I have deemed it worthwhile to include the words of my friend in this place:

> *First, I send here to Your Reverence a copy of a Magical Seal, which Ferdinand, Duke of Alcalá and Viceroy of Naples—a noble ornament of erudition—had cast some time ago in Naples; along with the description which I have taken care to subject on a sheet of transparent paper. It is now three years since I was teaching Philosophy in our College at Seville, <margin>The structure of the Talisman.</margin> when I first saw this bronze capsule with admiration (for it is shaped like the cases <note>original: "capsulam... ad instar thecarum"</note> in which the hosts for the sacrifices <note>The Eucharist</note> are kept among us), and then I considered it repeatedly several times. It is entirely empty inside, as the Duke himself proved by experiment when it was opened; and it hangs from a cord inserted through a celestial sign, in which a man is seen sitting upon a Ram <note>The zodiac sign Aries</note>. The four large serpents, which divide the imaginary and upper face, are cast metal; all other things are engraved with a chisel. At every strike that occurs on the upper part, a sharp sound rings out from within, like a little bell; the strikes of which can be distinguished and numbered, and indeed the tinkling can be perceived after the blow. I have often moderated my hand so that I struck with equal force; but that ambiguous sound never responded with an equal number of pulsations or strikes of the Bell. Often I even beat in the same place and with the same force, but the tinkling was never con-*

It was constant. I observed only one thing: the number of pulsations never exceeded thirty. Where the Duke obtained this monument of antiquity is obscure; some claim it was left by his grandfather, the **Marquis of Tarifa**, who undertook a pilgrimage to **Palestine**; others say it was a remnant of the household effects of **Henry, Marquis of Villena**, who is said to have lived in **Spain** two hundred years ago with a great reputation for **Magical** learning, of whom **Mariana** <note>Juan de Mariana (1536–1624), a famous Spanish historian.</note> writes in *Book 19, Chapter 8*. I listen to this latter account more willingly, because I know that **Villena** dealt in Hebrew and **Cabalistic** Magic, and possessed the *Raziel* <note>The *Sefer Raziel HaMalakh*, a medieval practical Kabbalah grimoire.</note> and other Magical books of that nation, which were burned in **Madrid** by order of King **John the Second of Castile**; from these, if I am not mistaken, the entire structure of this Seal was drawn. I compared the Neapolitan copy with the Original, and I discovered some things expressed more elegantly than faithfully. I took care that it be drawn by a **Painter** with a second review; and if he did not do so with great artistry, he certainly executed it with as much **precision in every detail** <note>original Greek: *κατ' ἀκρίβειαν ἁπάσας*</note> as he could. I had myself attempted (to hide nothing) an explanation of the characters; but as soon as I read through **Your Reverence's** *Prodromus* <note>Likely Kircher's *Prodromus Coptus* (1636).</note>, I preferred to reserve the entire matter for him who, by the genius and erudition in which he excels in other things, must be believed to be sufficient for himself in this part. I was persuading myself that it was a binding of the spirit of **Aries** (you know the masters of that ill-fated learning speak thus; they call them **bonds and constraints** <note>original Greek: *δέσμους καταδέσμους*</note> to us, and **Lucan** says they are "fettered"); I was explaining the precepts which they use for those bindings through types, characters, garlands, and the construction of celestial images, almost all of which I showed were expressed here. I was drawing the **Cabalistic** letters surrounding the images into my own interpretation, but I satisfied myself little in these, even if I pleased those not so skilled in such matters; for I am very little practiced in the Cabalistic matters of the Hebrews, nor have I tasted anything beyond what occurs in **Reuchlin**, **Agrippa**, and others, those **zealots of the magic arts** <note>original Greek: *ζηλωταῖς τεχνομάντων*</note>; hence it was necessary that we reasoned in a meager and dry fashion. I report these things so that **Your Reverence** may see and laugh at how I wandered astray, and how I have been relieved of a huge burden.

And this is the Magical structure, depicted quite skillfully by a friend. And although **Father Thomas de Leon** has "hit the needle on the head," as the saying goes, with his learned commentaries; it nevertheless seemed fit, on this so opportune an occasion, to interpose my own opinion, so that it may be clear to posterity what I judge concerning this Magical Seal.

<margin>Explanation of the Astrological Charm.</margin>
The structure is undoubtedly, as appears at first glance, Magical, nor does it smell of anything Egyptian, but is a device invented in later times by Mages, or rather by Satan. I do not include the figure in this work on purpose, both because I judged such a hateful and monstrous depiction of the Mages unworthy of the light, and lest I expend useless expense on such a harmful work, more worthy of the eternal darkness in which it was forged than of the public light. Countless Magical effigies of figures transformed by a certain exotic metamorphosis are seen here, and, lest any superstition be lacking, they are interspersed with the signs of the **Zodiac**, among which are everywhere interspersed Hebrew letters transformed in a strange way, under which are contained the names of powerful Demons, most fit for summoning them from the caverns of the underworld with imperious words. Around the Choir of Demonic figures, an inscription is seen poured out in a wide rotation in Hebrew characters, though strangely corrupted; under which, however, there is no trace of Hebrew, Chaldean, or Arabic speech...

Not a single trace [of meaning] remains hidden, as I have finally discovered through the greatest effort by means of the <term>combinatorial art</term> <note>A method of rearranging symbols or letters to find hidden meanings, popularized by Ramon Llull.</note>; instead, I found everything filled with portentous, barbaric, <term>unintelligible and unpronounceable</term> <note>original: ἀσήμοις καὶ ἀεκφωνήτοις</note> murmurs rather than words signifying anything. The four deformed dragons, transformed in a wondrous manner, signify nothing other than the hiding places and nesting sites of Demons distributed into the four parts of the World—that is, the Northern, Southern, Eastern, and Western Demons, with their surrounding followers under various disfigured forms.

<margin>The characters and inscription of the Talisman.</margin>
The surrounding inscription, written in mutilated Hebrew characters as I mentioned, offers to the entire army of Demons adjurations, incantations, and similar operations of impiety. By these, the invoked Demons would appear to fulfill their vows, giving answers to those consulting them either through a perceptible figure or through sensible signs. The sign was a number; the ringing of the Seal reported the number, and from that ringing, they gathered the information they sought. That this ringing is Magical, not Physical, is shown by the very structure of the Seal, which was hollow inside to receive a <term>familiar spirit</term> <note>original: πάρεδρον (paredron); a supernatural assistant or "assistant spirit" bound to the object.</note> enclosed therein by the force of a magical adjuration; this spirit warned its devotees about the matters questioned by means of ringings. If, for example, they were to consult the Eastern Demons at a certain competent Astrological hour and with such a sign ascending, they would direct the Satanic instrument, freely suspended, toward the East; and once the adjuration was performed, they awaited responses through the said signs. If they consulted Northern Demons, they suspended it freely toward the North, and then operated as before; and so on for the rest. All these things are evident from what we said above regarding the various types of divinations; for it was shown above in the section on Oracles that they most often gave responses to consultants through a certain occult ringing.

<margin>The Author of the Talisman.</margin>
As to who the Author of this might be, Father Thomas de Leon rightly believes it was cast by Villena, the most famous Magician of Spain, since these images and characters smell nothing of ancient superstitions, and the bronze appears more recent than to be called a casting from more than two hundred years ago. I therefore advise all who keep the figure of this Magical Oracle at home to hand it over to Vulcan <note>i.e., to burn or melt it down.</note>; for it can hardly be said how much calamity often befalls entire families because of keeping a thing consecrated to Demons, toward which they are always drawn as if to their own property, infesting men with wondrous illusions and horrendous deceptions. And this, among other reasons, was the sole reason why I thought it should not even be committed to print: for the Devil has a thousand arts and a thousand machinations for doing harm, with which, by the just judgment and permission of God, he agitates the hearts of mortals. And certainly, if I have ever seen a pernicious Magical Seal, I can rightly testify that this one is the most pernicious of all; therefore, let these words suffice for the Reader's caution.

*Hermanubis <note>A syncretic deity combining Hermes and Anubis, often serving as a messenger or guide</note>, minister of Osiris the lord of life and the providence of all things, guardian of the sacred Cistern.* From this it is clear that these hieroglyphics were engraved on the image in "running characters" <note>likely referring to Hieratic or Demotic script</note>, as they were commonly accustomed to do everywhere; we shall treat these in a specific Chapter in its proper place. # CHAPTER VIII.
## Concerning the Pythagorean Cabala.

<margin>Pythagorean Cabala.</margin>
**It is** so arranged, beyond the limits of nature, by the wits of curious men, that they ignorantly persuade themselves that all things presented to the senses are filled with divine mysteries and sacraments. They solidify their credulity with words drawn from Holy Scripture, while saying that God created all things in number, weight, and measure <note>A reference to Wisdom of Solomon 11:20, a foundational text for Christian and esoteric numerology</note>. They assert, therefore, that number is the most sacred of all things; and they superstitiously believe that number is implanted in every single letter of the alphabet, equally full of mysteries. From these letters, they believe names are formed, whose numbers—when resolved according to *isopsephy* <gloss>original: τὴν ἰσοψηφίαν; the practice of adding up the numerical values of letters in a word</gloss>—contain all the events of good or bad fortune. From this emerged that "notorious art" <margin>The Notorious Art.</margin> <note>The *Ars Notoria* was a medieval grimoire focused on rapid learning and memory through mystical figures and prayers</note>, by which they think they can judge the entire course of a life by resolving someone's name and surname into numbers. They call this art the Pythagorean Cabala, making Pythagoras its author—following the usual custom of such scoundrels, who seek to win some authority for their impostures by using the name of a great and famous man. I confess, however, that among all the efforts of this kind, I have found nothing more tasteless, more ridiculous, or resting on a more rotten foundation. Consequently, I cannot wonder enough how it is possible that many—even those who wish to appear wise and sensible in the eyes of men—can either have faith in this ill-fated art and utterly asinine philosophy, or can bring themselves to think they can achieve anything certain in the conjecture of future events by its help. But lest we seem to mock these fanatical trifles in vain, let us place before the eyes of the curious reader one or two examples of the worm-eaten structures of this Satanic doctrine.

First, these Pythagorean initiates—or rather, scoundrels—presume an alphabet written in Latin letters for the Latins, Italian for the Italians, Greek for the Greeks, and Arabic for the Arabs. There are, therefore, various alphabets which they abuse. <margin>Various alphabets of the Pythagorean Cabalists.</margin> The magician Cattanus <margin>Cattanus.</margin> <note>Pietro Cataneo, an Italian author who wrote on geomancy and fortunetelling in the 16th century</note> sets down this one in his ridiculous Geomancy:

| A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H | I | K | L | M | N | O | P | Q | R | S | T | V | X | Y | Z |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1. | 3. | 22. | 24. | 22. | 3. | 7. | 6. | 20. | 1. | 10. | 23. | 12. | 8. | 13. | 27. | 13. | 9. | 8. | 2. | 6. | 3. | 4. |

In this alphabet, you have the numerical value of each letter, which it is certain that either men or a Demon invented without reason; for why is unity assigned to the letter K, and the same to the letter A? Why 8 to the letter O, 12 to the letter N, and so on for the rest? When Cornelius Agrippa <margin>Cornelius Agrippa.</margin> <note>Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa (1486–1535), a famous occult philosopher whose "Three Books of Occult Philosophy" systematized much of this lore</note> noticed this insanity, he thought something more plausible should be established, and he arranged his "onomatomantic" alphabet—or more truly, "onomantic" <note>Divination based on the meaning or numerical value of names</note>—differently, as follows:

And he asserts this is that divine Pythagorean invention, and he praises Alexander the Philosopher for teaching the method by which the stars of the Horoscope and divining stars can be found from the numbers of the letters; each among...

...which of a husband and wife will die first, or who will survive the other: all of which things have absolutely no foundation in reason and are worthy of being laughed at even by children. Just as they are deservedly avoided by every true Christian as tasteless, foolish, sacrilegious, and Satanic works. But let us set forth an operation full of stupidity and madness.

<margin>The foolish use of Cabalistic Alphabets.</margin>
If you desire to know, they say, the ruling star of someone born, calculate his name and that of both parents letter by letter according to a prescribed number. Divide the sum collected from the whole by nine, subtracting that number as many times as you can; and if one or four remains, both indicate the Sun. If, however, two or seven remains, both designate the Moon; just as three denotes Jupiter; five, Mercury; six, Venus; eight, Saturn; and nine, Mars. To these things, men of shameless character <note>literally "men of a rubbed-off forehead," a Latin idiom for those who have lost the ability to blush</note> add that the Horoscope of a person can be found in this way: Let the name of the mother, the father, and the child be calculated, and the collected sum divided by twelve. For the remaining one signifies Aries; 2, Aquarius; <margin>Refutation.</margin> 3, Capricorn; 4, Cancer; 5, Leo; 6, Virgo; 7, Aries; 8, Libra; 9, Scorpio; 10, Sagittarius; 11, Pisces; 12, Gemini. And these are the hidden secrets of the architects of all wickedness, not to be revealed. But who, I ask, would believe these follies? Who would have faith in such utterly shameful trifles? For it would follow from this that all Peters, Jameses, Pauls, etc., since they result in the same numbers when resolved, would all be subject to one and the same constellation, and consequently would experience the same fortune. These men, moved in their minds not by reason but by fantastic and demonic mockeries, respond: 1. belongs to the Sun, because the Sun is one and alone; 2. to the Moon, which they say is endowed with both sexes and is the Soul of the World, to which they also attribute 4, because of the four corners of the world and the four seasons of the year which she discerns; 5. since it is composed of the first even and odd number, they say it belongs to Mercury, just as he is composed of female and male; 6. they wish to belong to Venus, because it is constituted from 2 and 3. Who would not laugh at such tasteless inventions? O blessed parents, upon whose whim it would depend that a son, by the mere imposition of a name, might soon be filled with every happiness of fortune through the favor of the planet ruling that name!

<margin>Another Alphabet of the Pythagorean Cabalists</margin>
To this Alphabet we subjoin another commonly used, by which "shadow-strutters" <note>original: "tenebriones," meaning swindlers or those who operate in darkness</note> of this kind persuade themselves—and foolishly boast—that they can give a perfect judgment concerning the life and character of those born, and all the lots of good or bad fortune. The alphabet follows:

| A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H | I | K | L | M | N | O | P | Q | R | S | T | V | X | Y | Z |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 3 | 22| 24| 22| 3 | 8 | 6 | 29| 10| 12| 23| 12| 8 | 13| 23| 13| 9 | 8 | 2 | 6 | 3 | 4 |

<margin>Refutation.</margin>
Here I would first ask: why do they assign three to A, or the same three to B, F, and Y? Why 22 to C and E? Why also assign 13 to P and R? And finally, why 23 to M and Q? These most lying conjurers twist themselves strangely in this place; nor can they assign to us any other foundation of reason than either the cooperation of a Demon, with whom they concluded a pact to decide this, or the phantom of a most dull brain driven mad by a Demon. To show this more clearly, I shall reveal it with examples. First, from the numerical sum assumed in the names, they take away 9 as many times as possible, and keep the remainder for themselves; then they contemplate those remainders; which, when compared together, they answer...

CHAPTER
VIII.
</margin>

They claim to determine whether this person or that person will survive, whether this one or that one will die first, or who will live longer, and other similar matters. But they do not achieve this simply by assuming that if one remainder is larger than the other, it immediately suggests victory; rather, they often promise the palm of victory and a longer life from a smaller number, just as they do from a larger one at other times. For example, the numbers 1 and 2 signify that the man who has the remainder of two in his name will be the victor, while the other who has 1 will be slain. Likewise, with 1 and 3, the 1 signifies that he will overcome when the adversary has a remainder of three; and so on for the rest. Yet these rules are compiled so stupidly that to whichever alphabet you apply them, they differ by "the whole heaven" <note>original: "toto cœlo"; a Latin idiom meaning "entirely" or "diametrically opposed."</note>. For instance, when a remainder of four and three is left between two men, the four ought to win; yet this is false in the names of Cain and Abel. The former has a remainder of three, and the latter a four; and yet, if the rules of the Name-Diviners <term>Onomatomantū: practitioners of Onomatomancy, the art of foretelling the future based on the numerical value of a person's name</term> were true, Abel should have overcome Cain—the contrary of which Holy Scripture asserts. The same appears in Absalom and Joab; the latter has a remainder of seven, the former five, and therefore he should have defeated Joab; yet Holy Scripture relates the opposite to us. It would likewise follow from these fanatical rules of name-divination that he who is defeated in Latin would win in French; who does not see how absurd this is? For if you consult—as Mersenne <note>Marin Mersenne (1588–1648), a French polymath and priest who wrote extensively against magic and alchemy</note> acutely demonstrates in his work on Genesis—a Name-Diviner skilled in the Latin language, he will immediately affirm that Mary will overcome Stephen, and live longer than him, because after subtracting the numbers of the name by 9, a remainder of 8 stays for Mary, but for Stephen, a three; for these triflers claim that three is overcome by eight. But let us set down an example. Let the said names be written, as appears to the side, to each of which you apply the corresponding number from the alphabet; with the numbers collected into one sum, you will see in Stephen the sum of 84; in Mary 71. Subtract 9 from these as many times as you can: in Mary’s name 8 will remain, and in Stephen’s name a three. From this they deduce that Mary is the victor and ought to live longer than Stephen. Truly, that this is most false will appear from the French names, from which the total opposite results, as can be seen in the French names *Marie* and *Estienne*; if you resolve these into numbers, you will have a sum of 136 for the latter and 90 for the former. When the number nine is rejected from these as many times as possible, it leaves 1 in the first and 9 in the second; and thus, contrary to the rules of Number-Divination <term>arithmomanticas: Arithmancy, divination using numbers</term>, *Mary*, who stood as the victor under the Latin name, will be overcome under the French name. But it is the custom of such impostors that when they see a matter has not turned out well, they pretend wondrous excuses—either that the process was not legitimate, or that something was omitted.

# EGYPTIAN OEDIPUS: THE HIEROGLYPHIC GYMNASIUM

<margin>CHAPTER VIII.</margin> Within the central cavity, three columns are distinguished by the diameter line A–B, filled with numbers. Those contained above the diameter A–B are called "fortunate" and "numbers of life"; those contained below the diameter A–B are named "unfortunate" and "numbers of death." For this reason, the former are usually painted in red and the latter in black. And such is the composition of that most wretched wheel, which I truly marvel has crept—by what deception I know not—even into the works of the *Venerable Bede* <note>A famous 8th-century English monk and scholar; the author, Kircher, is skeptical that such a superstitious device actually originated with him</note>. But let us explain its use.

<margin>Use of the Wheel.</margin> First, therefore, the Satanic high priests <note>original: "Archimystae Satanici"</note>, when about to consult on whether a matter is true or false, take the number of the letters of both parties involved in the business; also the number of the hour and the day on which the conversation is held; also the number of the month and the Zodiac sign. They collect all these into one sum and divide the sum by 30, then look for the remainder on the wheel. If the remainder is found above the diameter A–B among the red numbers, the truth of the matter is promised to them; but if the said remainder is found below the diameter A–B, the matter is proven to be a falsehood. Let us provide another example. When consulting whether someone in a remote region is alive or dead, they proceed thus: they take the number of the absent person's name, which they extract from the numerical alphabet in the two outermost circles; then the number of the month, together with the number of the days of the month on which he departed; and they collect these together into one sum, to which they add the number of the current year. They divide this total sum of numbers by 30, and if the remainder is found above the diameter A–B, they certainly pronounce him to be alive; if the same is found below the diameter A–B, they assert he is dead.

If they wish to know whether someone is to be released from prison or not, they take the number of the prisoner's name, and the year, month, and day on which he was made a captive; to these collected values they add the name of the city and country; and they divide the total sum by 30. If the remainder is found among the red numbers above the diameter A–B, he will be freed; if among the black, he will undergo death, as they believe.

<margin>Refutation of the Wheel of Life and Death.</margin> At this point, truly, much Hellebore <note>A plant used in antiquity as a treatment for madness or "clearing the brain"</note> would be needed to purge the insane brains of such foolish little "philosophers," so that they might learn to philosophize more rationally. For I can in no way discern what power or subtlety lies hidden in this ridiculous mechanism, unless perhaps they say that the Onomantic Alphabet <note>A system of divination based on the numerical value of names</note>, which was previously written in a straight line, now possesses a peculiar power when adapted into a circular form; who does not see how senseless that is? Furthermore, I can understand even less what mystery the seven planetary characters with their subscript numbers possess—having more power in a circle than when written in a straight line. Finally, I do not grasp why the red numbers above the diameter, written normally now and not circularly, should obtain more power for life than the lower black ones for death. I know that a club, whether turned upward or downward, surely possesses the same strength for striking; it is to be wished that the insane heads of these ill-omened diviners were soundly thrashed with such clubs, rather than words, so that they might finally be brought to their senses. But what of that confused collection of hour, day, month, names, sign, planet, and numbers...

He mocks the superstitious logic of the "philosophers" who believe that arranging numbers in a circle or changing their color grants them divinatory power.</summary>

## CHAPTER X.
->On the Geomancy of the Arabs.<-

<margin>Geomancy of the Arabs.</margin>
**A**nother deception arises from the superstitious doctrine of the Arabs, and it is Geomancy, which they call <term>حساب الرمل</term> *Hassab elrammel* <note>Literally "The Science of the Sand."</note>; by which, after a preliminary incantation, they rashly cast certain prayer-points onto paper. They stolidly persuade themselves that an occult Intelligence (or more truly, an Evil Spirit <note>original: "Cacocæmone"</note>) directs the hand of the one casting them. These foolish schemers believe they can gather the entire state of one's fortune by consulting the points in this manner. Some press the points into the earth, from which certain figures are drawn in even or odd numbers, which are then referred back to the signs of the heavens and assume their power and nature. Indeed, the points ought to be made in the earth with the index finger, because they think the hand of the painter is moved by terrestrial spirits. The author of Arabic Geomancy first assigned certain orders of points to letters, which they use in their divinations <note>original: "sortilegijs"</note>, as follows:
